529	
530	Assembly's arithmetic is small on purpose. The Graph owns the seam formulas (`seam_at_weld`, `A_seam_m`, the SEALED/RAGGED hole and open-end rates), Layout the weld offset and detach re-base, Body the docking invariant and `actors_overlapping`, Interaction the channel clock, ledger and subject budget. This section defines only what Assembly owns (`q`, the two offer predicates, host and mate selection, the cut-mode derivation, the pending TTL, the body-count bound, the shape-change time, the CASCADE deadline) and works each cited formula at MVP values so the numbers a reviewer sees are the numbers a test asserts. Every formula is integer arithmetic (the kernel's determinism rule: anything hashed, replicated or replayed is integer or fixed-point); the only fractional values below are display conversions marked as such. Numbering matches the cross-references in Detailed Design (D.2 to D.12 are cited there); D.13 to D.18 are additions. Every formula that Assembly owns is a registry candidate as a **formula** (name, expression, variables), not only as constants (`docs/consistency-failures.md`: register the formula). MVP data: the pair `sock_airlock_e` (home-ship, facing E, `line_px` 720, `start_px` 672) and `sock_b_w` (derelict B, facing W, `line_px` 24, `start_px` 288), `width_tiles` 2, lanes POWER 0 and O2 0, weld offset `(696, 384)` (DA-10), `GRID_24` closure. Where a value is not published by its owner it is marked `[UNV]`.
531	
532	### D.1 Weld quality
533	
534	The weld_quality formula is defined as:
535	
536	`q = clamp( WELD_Q_DEFAULT , Q_MIN , Q_MAX )`, with `Q_MIN = max(400, ceil(LEAK_HP / 10))` and `Q_MAX = 990`
537	
538	Derived: `Q_MIN` is the larger of 400 and the smallest `q` whose `hp_seam = q x 10` (`LSG D.14`) is not below `LEAK_HP` (that smallest `q` is `ceil(LEAK_HP / 10)`, so a `LEAK_HP` that is not a multiple of 10 rounds up and the integer-division ambiguity does not arise; the 400 outer floor holds across the Graph's 2000-6000 `LEAK_HP` range); `Q_MAX` is the registered 990, 3 permille under the first `q` (993) at which the Graph's weep is 0 from birth (`LSG D.2`, floor form) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: re-justified; the earlier "10 permille under the q = 1000 cliff" came from the superseded ceiling form. Q_MAX stays 990, a registered value, but a weld at Q_MAX now weeps only 2 milli flow units for about 6.3 minutes, so it is the faintest legal weld, not a still-weeping one)*. The clamp runs once, at data load, never per weld; a clamped value raises the diagnostic `MSA_Q_CLAMPED`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **this is the one place the range of `q` is stated**: `Q_MIN(LEAK_HP)` to 990, which is 400 to 990 at the default `LEAK_HP` 4000 and 600 to 990 at 6000. Every other mention (MSA-13, T9, T17, FB-8, VA-15) cites D.1.)* The rule has no other term: there is no `sum q_mods`, no per-weld input and no state read.
539	
540	**Variables:**
541	
542	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
543	|---|---|---|---|---|
544	| `WELD_Q_DEFAULT` | int (permille) | 400-990, default 850 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | data file (registry candidate ★) | The one weld-quality constant; refines advisor R11 (was 400-1000) |
545	| `LEAK_HP` | int (bp) | 2000-6000, default 4000 | Graph tuning (cited, locked) | Below this a fluid sub-edge starts in LEAK |
546	| `Q_MIN` | int (permille) | 400-600 (400 at `LEAK_HP` <= 4000; 600 at 6000) | derived | Lower clamp; moves with `LEAK_HP`, never below 0 |
547	| `Q_MAX` | int (permille) | 990 | derived (`1000 - 10`) | Upper clamp |
548	| `q` | int (permille) | `Q_MIN`..990 | calculated | The value placed in the plan handed to `weld_join` and stored on the SeamRecord |
549	
550	**Output Range:** 400 to 990 inclusive. Two named cliffs sit just outside it. *Below 400:* `hp_seam` falls under `LEAK_HP` and every fluid sub-edge of the seam starts in LEAK mode, a leak with no prior tell (a P2 fairness break). *At q 993 and above (1000 is the limiting case):* `A_seam_m` is 0 from the first period, the seam has no weep and the weld loses its P1 tell *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. `A_seam_m` is the Graph's (`LSG D.2`) and falls linearly with `leak_bp`, which wears in by 100 bp per 10 s period from 10000 (`leak_bp = 10000 - 100 x period`); the table is worked at registry defaults for `L_seam` 2 and states no expression. Within the range the Graph's consequences are physical and cited, not restated (below, `L_seam` 2, cable port caps 3000):
551	
552	| `q` | `(500 + q/2)` permille of the lesser port | `cap_seam` (W) | `hp_seam` | `A_seam_m` at period 0 (milli flow units, `L_seam` 2) | `A_seam_m` at period 50 | weep ends | verdict |
553	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
554	| 399 (loaded as-is, would clamp to 400) | 699 | 2097 | 3990 (below `LEAK_HP` 4000) | 11,558 | 5,778 | period 100 | leaks at birth: outside the range |
555	| 400 | 700 | 2100 | 4000 (not below) | 11,520 | 5,760 | period 100 | the lower bound |
556	| 700 | 850 | 2550 | 7000 (`HP_OK` boundary) | 2,880 | 1,440 | period 100 | legal, tight |
557	| 850 | 925 | 2775 | 8500 | 720 | 360 | period 100 (about 16.7 min) | the MVP default |
558	| 990 | 995 | 2985 | 9900 | 2 | 0 | period 38 (about 6.3 min) | the upper bound: a faint, short weep |
559	| 1000 (loaded as-is, would clamp to 990) | 1000 | 3000 | 10000 | 0 | 0 | none | no weep at birth: outside the range |
560	
561	**Example:** the data file ships `WELD_Q_DEFAULT = 850`: no clamp, `q = 850`, `MSA_Q_CLAMPED` not raised. A modder or a bad edit ships 1000: the loader clamps to 990, raises `MSA_Q_CLAMPED` once at load, the weld produces `A_seam_m` 2 at period 0 (a faint weep that ends at period 38, about 6.3 minutes) and the Graph's descriptor keeps `intensity_pm` at least 1 while it flows (LS-14) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
562	
563	### D.2 Offer predicates
564	
565	The weld_offer formula is defined as:
566	
567	`weld_offer(seat, s) = ( tool_in_hand(seat) == tool_welder ) AND lit(seat, s) AND in_reach(seat, s) AND ( socket_state(s) == FREE ) AND ( |Pairs(s)| >= 1 )`, with `Pairs(s) = { (a, b) : s IN {a, b} AND host_of(a, b) AND can_attach(a, b) == OK AND docked(a, b, frame_shift_px(a, b)) }` and `host_of` the host rule of D.3 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier form defined `weld_offer` through a host socket `a` that D.3 defined through the same candidate set; the focused socket `s` now seeds the candidate pairs and D.3 only chooses among them)*
568	
569	Derived: the prompt `E . Weld` exists iff `weld_offer` is true. The predicate reads no node or edge accessor, calls neither `can_join_static` nor the full `can_join`, and reads no `surge[]` (MSA-9, MSA-12). The carry lockout (a seat carrying an item gets no channelled verb, PC-7, IA-28) is Interaction's selector, not a term here; a carrying seat therefore never sees the weld prompt and `begin_weld` is a `BUSY` backstop.
570	
571	**Variables:**
572	
573	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
574	|---|---|---|---|---|
575	| `tool_in_hand(seat)` | enum | tool class id | Suit (`tool_welder` is class {1, 9}, slot 2, equipped at start) | The equipped tool |
576	| `lit(seat, s)` | bool | 0 or 1 | Emitter State via Interaction's lit check | The socket subject is lit (lit-only channelled verbs, PC-7) |
577	| `in_reach(seat, s)` | bool | 0 or 1 | Interaction reach geometry, `REACH_PX` 72 | The socket subject is within reach |
578	| `socket_state(s)` | enum | `FREE`, `WELDED`, `CAPPED`, `CUT_OPEN` | Layout (LY-13) | Terminal lifecycle (S3) |
579	| `can_attach(a, b)` | enum | `OK` or one of eight reasons | Layout (LY-14) | The mating verdict |
580	| `frame_shift_px(a, b)` | int pair (px) | on the 24-px grid | Layout `LY D.6` (ASK L3 asks for it as a pure read) | The shift the weld would apply (D.5) |
581	| `docked(a, b, fs)` | bool | 0 or 1 | Body `BDY D.8` | The two bodies already sit at the weld offset with equal velocity |
582	| `Pairs(s)` | set of ordered socket pairs `(a, b)` | 0..`MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION` x `MAX_SECTIONS` in principle; exactly 0 or 1 in MVP | calculated | The ordered pairs that contain the focused socket `s`, put in host order by D.3, and pass both `can_attach` and `docked` |
583	| `weld_offer` | bool | 0 or 1 | calculated | Whether the prompt exists |
584	
585	**Output Range:** boolean. Pure and total: no side effect, no module-body state. In MVP `|Pairs|` is 0 or 1 by authoring (one socket pair); with several candidate pairs `[VS]` D.3 selects the lowest key pair. Per-call cost is O(1) over cached static data (`MSA_WELD_OFFER_BUDGET_US`, set in the spike).
586	
587	**Example:** the seat holds the welder, stands lit within 72 px of `sock_airlock_e`; the socket is `FREE`; `sock_b_w` passes `can_attach` (facings E and W are opposite, `width_tiles` 2 and 2, `SOCKET_CLASS` 1 and 1, lane multisets equal, no `GEOM_OVERLAP` under Layout's `rects_in` test: the home `spine_corridor` east hull wall is x [672, 696) per Derelict Authoring D.13); B is docked at `frame_shift_px = (696, 384)`: `|Pairs| = 1`, offer = 1, the prompt shows. The same stance with B still 24 px short of its dock (`world(b) - world(a) = (720, 384)`): `docked` is false, `|Pairs| = 0`, offer = 0, **no prompt and no "can't weld" icon**.
588	
589	The seam_cut_offer formula is defined as:
590	
591	`seam_cut_offer(seat, s) = ( tool_in_hand(seat) == tool_cutter ) AND lit(seat, s) AND in_reach(seat, s) AND ( socket_state(s) == WELDED ) AND ( seam_state(seam_of(s)) == ACTIVE ) AND ( foot_section(seat) IN keep_sections(seam_of(s)) )`
592	
593	Derived: `keep_sections` is the component of the weld forest that keeps its `body_id` (the one containing the body's `origin_section_id`, LY-17; in MVP the home-ship side), from Layout's `detach_preview` (ASK L1). There is deliberately **no `CUT_BLOCKED` term**: the prompt is offered, `CUT_BLOCKED` is checked at begin, handoff and completion (D.13), and the clean hatch-presence oracle stays a rejection the player can see (MSA-21).
594	
595	**Variables:**
596	
597	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
598	|---|---|---|---|---|
599	| `tool_in_hand(seat)` | enum | tool class id | Suit (`tool_cutter`, class {8}, slot 1) | The equipped tool |
600	| `lit`, `in_reach` | bool | 0 or 1 | as above | |
601	| `socket_state(s)` | enum | as above | Layout | Must be `WELDED` |
602	| `seam_of(s)` | seam id | `seam_id` allocated by the Graph | Layout `welds[]` | The seam the socket is part of |
603	| `seam_state` | enum | `ACTIVE`, `CUT` | Layout / Graph | Only an `ACTIVE` seam can be cut |
604	| `foot_section(seat)` | section id | a section of the seat's body | Body `BDY D.10` | The section containing the seat's foot **origin** (BDY-23) |
605	| `keep_sections(seam)` | set of section ids | 1..`MAX_SECTIONS` | Layout `detach_preview` (ASK L1) | Sections that keep `body_id` after the cut |
606	
607	**Output Range:** boolean. **Example:** welded pair, seat standing in the home-ship airlock (a section in the home component): offer = 1. The same seat standing in derelict B's `b_dock`: `foot_section` is in the leaving component, offer = 0 and **no cut prompt exists on the derelict side** (the self-strand trap is unreachable). A `FREE` socket: offer = 0 (state must be `WELDED`); a `CAPPED` socket: offer = 0 (terminal).
608	
609	### D.3 Host and mate selection
610	
611	The host_and_mate formula is defined as:
612	
613	`host_of(a, b) = ( kind(sec(a)) == HOME AND kind(sec(b)) == DERELICT )` ; `(socket_a, socket_b) = argmin over Pairs(s) of ( socket_key_a , socket_key_b )` in that lexicographic order, with `Pairs(s)` as in D.2; the pair is empty when `Pairs(s)` is empty *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the section variable is renamed `sec` so `s` means only a socket; the focused socket seeds `Pairs(s)`; and the tie-break over candidate pairs is stated)*
614	
615	Derived: if both sections are DERELICT `[VS]`, `host_of` instead holds for the ordering whose `socket_a` is on the body with the lower `body_id`. **When the HOME section has several sockets** `[VS]`, a seat focusing a derelict socket `s` has one candidate pair per FREE HOME socket that passes `can_attach` and `docked`, and the pair with the lowest `socket_key_a` wins, then the lowest `socket_key_b`; a seat focusing a HOME socket has `socket_a = s` and the tie-break runs over the mates. In the MVP there is one pair, so no tie-break fires. The seat may stand on either side and focus either socket; Assembly derives the ordered pair, so the surviving body is always the home-ship's and the absorbed derelict body is re-based (LY-16 / LY Open Question 21: confirmed).
616	
617	**Variables:**
618	
619	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
620	|---|---|---|---|---|
621	| `kind(s)` | enum | `HOME`, `DERELICT` | Graph LS-17 | Section kind |
622	| `body_id` | int | 0..`MAX_BODIES` - 1 | Layout | The tie-break for a two-derelict pair `[VS]` |
623	| `socket_key` | string id | stable, ordered by byte comparison | Layout | The tie-break among several candidate pairs `[VS]` |
624	| `sec(x)` | section id | a section of the loaded set | Layout | The section a socket belongs to *(renamed from the reused `s`, re-review)* |
625	| `Pairs(s)` | set | as D.2 | calculated | Candidate ordered pairs containing the focused socket |
626	
627	**Output Range:** one ordered pair `(socket_a, socket_b)` or the empty pair (no offer). Deterministic: the same state always selects the same pair, which replay and MIRROR rely on. **Example:** the seat stands in derelict B's `b_dock` and focuses `sock_b_w`; `kind(derelict_b)` is DERELICT, `kind(home_ship)` is HOME; the pair is `(sock_airlock_e, sock_b_w)` regardless of which socket was focused, and B is the absorbed side.

710	`T_done = Tb + D - resume_offset` ; `T_apply = T_done + 1` ; `blocks = D / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` ; `exposure_s = ( D - resume_offset ) / TICK_RATE` ; `tool_pushes = D - resume_offset` ; constraint `D mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS == 0`

712	Derived: the clock, the abort set, the ledger and the noise are Interaction's (IA-14, IA-16, IA-33); Assembly supplies only `D` and consumes `T_done`. Accrual is at `e = T - Tb` = 1 to `D - resume_offset`, so the DONE handoff is the P3 of tick `T_done` and the completion applies in the P2 of `T_apply` (MSA-3). `resume_offset = blocks_done x B` while the ledger entry is valid (`T - abort_tick <= PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`), else 0 (`IA D.6`, cited). 810	### D.12 Weld notification batch
811	
812	The weld_batch_key_budget formula is defined as:
813	
814	`keys_block = base_block + n_moved + n_actors + n_subject_deltas <= MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` ; checked per block, for each of `graph.state`, `layout.state`, `body.state`, `interaction.state`, `assembly.state`
815	
816	Derived: the kernel batches one notification per block (CR-10). The Graph's batch is fixed by its owner (`T`, `S/<seam_id>`, `SEC/<a>`, `SEC/<b>`, nothing else); Layout adds `SEC/` and `BODY/` keys for moved sections; Body adds pose and actor keys; Interaction adds only subjects whose registration changed (ASK I1(vii)). Exceeding `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` collapses a block's batch to `ALL` and costs a full rebuild, so the budget is checked, not assumed.
817	
818	**Variables:**
819	
820	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
821	|---|---|---|---|---|
822	| `base_block` | int | graph 4; layout 5; body 2; interaction 0; assembly 1 per seat that changed | the owners' key sets | Fixed keys |
823	| `n_moved` | int | MVP 1 (derelict B); worst case <= `MAX_SECTIONS` 24 | Layout | Sections whose offset changed |
824	| `n_actors` | int | 0..`MAX_ACTORS` 8 | Body | Actors transferred by BM3 or BM4 |
825	| `n_subject_deltas` | int | MVP <= 4 (door faces) | Interaction `sync_section` | Subjects whose registered state changed |
826	| `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` | int | 256 | Kernel (cited, locked) | Collapse threshold |
827	
828	**Output Range:** MVP weld: `graph.state` 4; `layout.state` <= 6 (the moved section's `SEC/` key coincides with `SEC/<b>`, so 5 is the likely union and 6 the bound); `body.state` <= 3 with one avatar (2 pose rows + 1 actor; <= 10 only at the `MAX_ACTORS` 8 cap); `interaction.state` <= 4; `assembly.state` <= 1 (one key per changed seat; only the welder's seat changes in an MVP weld). Worst case `layout.state` 5 + 24 = 29. All well under 256. **The one failure mode** is `sync_section` marking every subject of both sections (about 98 + 98 fixtures plus loose items and stubs, up to about 190 in the three-section case), which is why the ask is "mark only changed subjects". **Example:** home + B weld with one avatar on B: graph 4, layout 6, body 2 + 1 = 3, interaction 4, assembly 1: five batches, the largest 6 keys. Conservation and fresh-seam disconnection on the apply tick are asserted by the Graph itself (LS-24) and cross-checked by AC-MSA-25 and AC-MSA-67; they are not re-owned here.

830	### D.13 Hatch-cap check (`CUT_BLOCKED`)
831	
832	The cut_blocked formula is defined as:
833	
834	`rects(seam) = { hatch_rect_a , hatch_rect_b }` with each of size `( WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH ) x ( width_tiles x TILE_PX )` in the body frame ; `cut_blocked = ( actors_overlapping( body_id , rects(seam) ) != empty )` with `ov( box , r ) = max(0, min(x1) - max(x0)) x max(0, min(y1) - max(y0)) > 0`
835

The list includes the cutter. The geometry guarantee that the cutter's own foot box can stand outside both rectangles within reach is a Layout and Authoring requirement (`SOCKET_STANCE_BAND_EMPTY`, ASK L2), not an Assembly term.

839	
840	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
841	|---|---|---|---|---|

867	### D.15 Apply budget split
868	
869	The apply_budget_split formula is defined as:
870	
871	`weld_apply_ms = m2 + lm2 + bm3 + 2 x sync + own + verifier_release <= MSA_WELD_APPLY_BUDGET_MS` ; `cut_apply_ms` has the same shape with `m3 + lm3 + bm4`; `install_apply_ms = check + m5 + release + clear + sync + own <= MSA_INSTALL_APPLY_BUDGET_MS`
872	
873	Derived: a documentation formula. The spike reports each term separately so that a failed budget points at an owner. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **the 0.5 ms split is an allocation target, not a measurement, and it is optimistic for GDScript.** The example below implies well under a microsecond per synced subject (0.10 ms for two sections of roughly a hundred subjects each), which is native-code speed; an interpreted GDScript loop with dictionary access is plausibly 3 to 5 times slower, so a spike that fails 0.5 ms would be a false negative about the design. Rules: (1) a micro-benchmark S0 runs first and measures the per-call cost of a representative mutator, a `sync_section` over 100 subjects and the release verifier subset in GDScript on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK (R12), and the term budgets and `MSA_*_APPLY_BUDGET_MS` are **re-derived from S0** before S1 is judged; (2) the S1 fallback (splitting the apply across ticks behind a Graph-held "welding" state) triggers **only if the whole weld tick (P2 plus P3) exceeds `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4**, the kernel's logging threshold, never merely because the 0.5 ms allocation is missed; (3) the per-term budgets stay as gating criteria on the named reference machines, pending spike measurement on RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK (Open Question 6, closed by R12).)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the per-term budgets are **reported, not gated**; the one gate is the whole weld tick under `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 (AC-MSA-23). A re-derived budget is frozen by a committed change before the run that judges it, and is capped at 2.0 ms, the knob's safe-range ceiling, unless the user signs off a higher figure.)* The Graph's M2 alone is locked at <= 0.2 ms Release and sits inside the weld term.

875	**Variables:**
876	
877	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
878	|---|---|---|---|---|
879	| `m2`, `m3`, `m5` | float ms | `m2` <= 0.2 (locked) | Graph | Mutator cost |
880	| `lm2`, `lm3` | float ms | allocation targets, `[UNV]` | Layout | Mutator cost |
881	| `bm3`, `bm4` | float ms | `[UNV]`; up to `MAX_ACTORS` 8 transfers | Body | Mutator cost |
882	| `sync` | float ms | `[UNV]` | Interaction `sync_section` | One section re-registration |

889	### D.16 Fault loss window
890	
891	The fault_loss_window formula is defined as:
892	
893	`fault_loss_ticks = T_fault - last_save_T` ; `fault_loss_ticks <= AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS + AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` (10800 + 7200 = 18000 ticks, 5 minutes: the interval autosave is soft-gated, for example while `CHANNELLING` (SL-5), and a soft-blocked interval save may defer up to `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 7200 before it is written anyway, so this sum is the ceiling); enabling the `ASSEMBLY_WELD` / `ASSEMBLY_CUT` events can only shorten the window, never lengthen it. The name is distinct from Save/Load's registered `loss_ticks` (`T_dead - T_g`, the death-rule loss), which measures a different quantity
894	
895	Derived: a defect inside an Assembly `apply` moves the kernel `RUNNING -> FAULTED` (CR-9), and the only exit is a player-initiated restore of the last autosave. This is the price of "no rollback" stated as a number so a reviewer can accept or reject it. It is **not** the death rule (SL-7); it shares only the loading path.
896	
897	**Variables:**
898	
899	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
900	|---|---|---|---|---|
901	| `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` | int ticks | 10800 | Save/Load (cited) | Interval autosave |
902	| `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS` | int ticks | 1800 | Save/Load (cited) | Event coalescing floor (events can only add saves at least this far apart) |
903	| `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` | int ticks | 7200 | Save/Load (registry) | Longest wait of a soft-blocked interval save; after it the save is written anyway and tagged RISKY |
904	| `T_fault`, `last_save_T` | int64 ticks | | kernel; Save/Load | Tick of the defect; tick of the last autosave |
905	
906	**Output Range:** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the figures are relabelled. 10800 was called "typical" but it is a maximum: a defect lands uniformly inside the autosave interval, so the **mean** loss is about half of it.)* 0 to 18000 ticks (5 minutes of play) at the ceiling when a soft gate defers the interval save to `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS`; **maximum 10800 ticks (3 minutes) and mean about 5400 ticks (1.5 minutes)** when no soft gate defers it; with events enabled the window shrinks toward the event save but is not computed here. **Example:** a defect in A3 of a weld 2 minutes (7200 ticks) after the last interval autosave: the player loses up to 7200 ticks of play, within the 10800 maximum and the 18000 ceiling (*Amended 2026-10-27 — design review:* the soft-gate fixture of AC-MSA-148 deliberately lands a fault at `fault_loss_ticks` = 17999, the largest value the formula allows, so the 18000 path is exercised and not only the 7200 case); the existing save file is never overwritten while FAULTED. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions) (D55): the window, mean about 5400, maximum 10800, ceiling 18000 ticks, is accepted. With the weld and cut event saves shipping in the MVP (D17) the window for a defect after a completed weld or cut shrinks toward the event save (the minimum gap is `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS` 1800), and the RAGGED withhold and soft gate of MSA-33 cannot raise the ceiling because the soft gate is bounded by `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 7200.)*
907	
908	### D.17 Outcome cue gate
909	
910	The outcome_cue_gate formula is defined as:
911	
912	`cue_plays(p) = ( p == local_seat ) AND ( last_result[p] != NONE ) AND ( ( p , last_result[p].T ) != last_seen ) AND ( T_now - last_result[p].T <= OUTCOME_CUE_WINDOW_TICKS )` ; `last_seen` is initialised on join and on restore to the `(p , last_result[p].T)` found at that moment *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the `last_result[p] != NONE` conjunct is evaluated first, so an empty `last_result` after a restore or a join is never subtracted from; without it the result depended on how GDScript treats the empty record and on evaluation order) (Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: keyed by `(PlayerId, T)`, local seat only, initialised on join and restore; the registry expression `cue_plays = (last_result.T != last_seen_T) AND (T_now - last_result.T <= OUTCOME_CUE_WINDOW_TICKS)` is superseded, see the registry request)*
913	
914	Derived: presentation consumes `last_result` once. `last_result` is runtime-only (MSA-4), so a restore leaves it empty and never replays a cue; a MIRROR join never plays a stale one **because `last_seen` is initialised to the value found at join** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, not because of any clearing step: with `last_seen` unset the old formula would have played a result that was 30 ticks old at join. The outcome is presented by the verb family's one cue (MSA-34); the DONE outcome has its own completion cues (the bead locks, the burn-through).
915	
916	**Variables:**
917	
918	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
919	|---|---|---|---|---|
920	| `last_result[p].T` | int64 tick | >= 0 | `assembly.state` (runtime-only) | Presenter dedupe key, with `p` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
921	| `last_seen` | pair `(PlayerId, int64 tick)` | | presenter-local, not sim state | The last `(p, T)` the presenter acted on; initialised on join and restore *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
922	| `local_seat` | PlayerId | | the presenter's own seat binding | Cues play for the local seat only *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
923	| `T_now` | int64 tick | | kernel | Current tick |
924	| `OUTCOME_CUE_WINDOW_TICKS` | int ticks | 12-180, default 60 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | data file | Staleness bound |
925	
926	**Output Range:** boolean per presenter per `last_result` change. **Example:** a `NOT_TAKEN` is written at `last_result.T` = 437412; the presenter last saw 437000; the frame at 437420 has `T_now - last_result.T` = 8 <= 60: the cue plays once. A frame at 437500 after a hitch: 88 > 60, no cue (a stale cue after a hitch would read as a new failure). After a restore `last_result` is empty and no cue plays: the `!= NONE` conjunct is false and `T_now - last_result[p].T` is never evaluated *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **Join example** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a MIRROR client joins at tick 437442 and finds `last_result[1].T` = 437412 (30 ticks old, inside the 60-tick window); `last_seen` is initialised to `(1, 437412)`, so `cue_plays` is false and nothing plays; the next result at 437600 differs and plays once. A result of a crewmate (`p` = 2) never plays a cue on seat 1.
927	
928	### D.18 Welded-body capacity bounds
929	
930	The welded_body_capacity formula is defined as:
931	
932	`C_welded = sum over sections s in body of compartments(s) <= 12` (the Graph's LS-26 bound, read as the welded body, advisor R26) ; `nodes_loaded <= MAX_GRAPH_NODES` ; `edges_loaded + plan_edges <= MAX_GRAPH_EDGES`
933	
934	Derived: Assembly reads LS-26's "<= 12 compartments at the weld" as the **welded body's** compartment count (advisor R26). Whether LS-26 also bounds the loaded set `{home+B, A}` is the Graph's call (ASK G4). `CAPACITY` is a `can_join_static` reason; at MVP scale it is not at risk.
935	
936	**Variables:**
937	
938	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
939	|---|---|---|---|---|
940	| `compartments(s)` | int | per template | Layout / Authoring | Home 5, derelict A 4, derelict B 5 |
941	| `MAX_GRAPH_NODES`, `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` | int | 4096, 8192 | Graph (cited, locked) | Capacity |
942	| `plan_edges` | int | MVP 3 (1 OPENING + 1 CABLE + 1 DUCT), provisional on the Graph's plan shape | `socket_plan` | Edges the weld adds (nothing else) |
943	
944	**Output Range:** boolean lint. **Example:** home 5 + B 5 = `C_welded` 10 <= 12; the loaded set including A is 14 (ASK G4). Graph load: about 105 nodes of 4096 and a few hundred edges of 8192 (the Graph's own estimate), plus 3 edges for the weld.

947	
948	Grouped by theme. Each case states the exact outcome and the rule that decides it. "Site 1/2/3" are the three call sites of the one predicate (MSA-7); "the sputter" is the weld family's one non-DONE cue and "the gutter" the cut family's (MSA-34). Ids `E-n` are stable references for the Acceptance Criteria.
949	
950	### Zero, maximum and out-of-range values
951	
952	- **E-1. If the data file ships `WELD_Q_DEFAULT` 1000 or 399**: the loader clamps it to 990 or 400 at load, raises `MSA_Q_CLAMPED` once, and every weld uses the clamped value (D.1). Playing on a q-1000 weld (or any q of 993 or more) would delete the weld's weep (the P1 tell) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; playing on a q-399 weld would leak at birth with no tell (a P2 break). The clamp runs at load, never per weld, so no weld can disagree with another.
953	- **E-2. If `WELD_CHANNEL_TICKS` or `SECTION_CUT_CHANNEL_TICKS` is not a multiple of `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6, or is outside 240-480**: the data lint fails at boot and the game does not start with that file (IA I-2 and the analogy to I-9). A channel that does not span whole Graph blocks would credit a partial block, and a duration below 240 would leave the LONG bar class.
954	- **E-3. If `PENDING_TTL_TICKS` is outside 8-119**: `pending_ttl_ok` (D.11) is false and the boot lint fails. Below 8 a legitimate completion held back by the kernel's per-tick truncation would be `STALE`; at 120 or above a completion could outlive a begin's own age window *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
955	- **E-4. If a `plan` would take the welded body above 12 compartments or the Graph above `MAX_GRAPH_NODES` 4096 or `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` 8192**: `can_join_static` returns `CAPACITY` at site 1 and the player gets the standard rejection cue (structural reasons are IMMEDIATE). The MVP welded body is 10 compartments and about 105 of 4096 nodes, so this is an authoring defect in MVP, not a play outcome (D.18).
956	- **E-5. If a `begin_*` is pressed while `assembly.state.pending.kind != NONE` for that seat**: it is rejected `BUSY` at site 1 and nothing is queued or opened. This BUSY gate is the single guarantee (D.11) that makes it impossible for a new handoff to meet an unresolved `pending`: the completion of the previous channel has either applied or resolved to `NOT_TAKEN` within 13 ticks, and the gate holds on a resumed begin too, whose channel can be as short as 6 ticks (D.7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
957	- **E-6. If the simulation runs with zero seats (a headless test, a menu state)**: `assembly.step` iterates an empty map, submits nothing and costs the idle budget only; `assembly.state` is `default_state()`. No Assembly path assumes a seat exists.
958	
959	### Simultaneous and ordering cases
960	
961	- **E-7 `[VS-B]` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. If two seats stand at the two different sockets of the one pair and both reach DONE on the same tick**: `assembly.step` submits two `weld` completions in ascending PlayerId order; the first applies; the second's `validate` fails `SOCKET_NOT_FREE` (both sockets are already `WELDED`), the command is Rejected, `pending` stays set and the second seat's outcome resolves as `NOT_TAKEN` at `submit_T + 13` with the weld sputter. Never a fault. The same socket cannot be contended at all: IA-34 gives the second seat `BUSY` at begin (one job per subject and verb class), so a double DONE needs the two *different* sockets (MSA-11 allows either to be focused); optional ASK I1(x) would close even that.
962	- **E-8 `[VS-B]` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. If the two seats' DONEs fall on consecutive ticks**: the second seat's handoff pre-check (site 2) sees the sockets `WELDED` and writes `REJECTED(SOCKET_NOT_FREE)`, submitting nothing, with the weld sputter. If the first completion is still queued (backlog), both completions are submitted and the first-queued applies, the other becomes `NOT_TAKEN` as in E-7. The welded state is single in every ordering (AC-MSA-59).
963	- **E-9. If a weld or cut applies in the same tick as a Graph hook tick (power `T mod 6 = 0`, atmo 2, failure 4)** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: the apply runs in P2 and the due Graph hook in P3, so the first Graph hook that runs after the apply refreshes the topology (Graph phase 1 refresh at the head of any hook) and sees the bumped `topology_version` and the new seam; no half-state is observable. Assembly neither registers nor orders against the Graph's hooks.
964	- **E-10. If an earlier command in the same P2 queue changes the target (a crewmate's salvage completion removes `j_b_main`)**: P2 order is `(queued_tick, host_order)`, so the earlier command applies first; the weld's `validate` then sees the new state, and the full `can_join` in step A0 reads `PORT_ABSENT`. The result is `BLOCKED(PORT_ABSENT)`: both orderings are legal and deterministic.
965	- **E-11. If a breach opens in either section during the weld channel**: the channel does not abort (the abort set is closed, IA-15) and the weld still applies; the new seam opens with hatch area 0, so nothing crosses until the player opens the hatch, and the full `can_join` at apply step A0 reports the larger `surge[]` (no Assembly presenter reads it; the creak is the Graph's `SEAL_STRAIN` descriptor, VA-16), never a number. The player who wants to patch first simply moves: the ledger holds the progress for `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` 600.
966	- **E-12 `[VS-B]` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. If a crewmate stands on the absorbed (derelict B) side in an unrelated channel when a weld applies** (the single-player form is the welder's own case, E-56): BM3 transfers every actor on the absorbed body, which counts as a body transfer, so the Controller clears their `channel_ref` and Interaction aborts their channel with cause `BODY`, crediting any finished blocks (IA-14 row 1). No special case in Assembly; the welder on B sees no displacement when `docked` held.
967	- **E-13. If a crewmate (or any other actor, in the MVP a Body double) steps into a hatch rectangle during a seam-cut channel** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (`[VS-B]` as co-op play; the double-based form gates the MVP, AC-MSA-36): the channel continues (a hazard is not an abort cause) and, at DONE, site 2 finds `actors_overlapping` non-empty and writes `REJECTED(CUT_BLOCKED)` with the gutter; the `LOUD` already went out at DONE, the seam stays welded and nothing is submitted. If the crewmate enters in the single tick between the handoff (P3 of `T_done`) and the completion (P2 of `T_apply`), site 3 rejects instead and the seat resolves as `NOT_TAKEN` 13 ticks after submission, with the same cue. "The ship will not close a seam on a crewmate" holds at all three sites.
968	- **E-14. If the cutter's own foot box overlaps a hatch rectangle**: the cut prompt is still offered (`seam_cut_offer` has no `CUT_BLOCKED` term, D.2) and begin is rejected `CUT_BLOCKED` with the standard rejection cue; stepping back out of the rectangle restores a valid begin. This is why Layout and Authoring must guarantee a legal stance at least one foot-box half-extent outside both rectangles within `REACH_PX` 72 (ASK L2, AC-MSA-37); without it the cut would be permanently self-blocked.
969	
970	### Target and state changes during the channel
971	
972	- **E-15. If the target lane node is salvaged before or during the weld channel (`j_main` or `j_b_main`, both def-backed; the bare `dj_*` nodes cannot be salvaged, DA-19)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: in MVP content this is meant to be unreachable, because ASK D2 authors the seam-lane node modules non-salvageable (MSA-8); the case stays specified for the Vertical Slice, for a defect and for the test fixture of AC-MSA-11: begin and the handoff pass (module-body state is never read there), the completion `validate` passes, and step A0 reads `PORT_ABSENT`: `last_result = BLOCKED(PORT_ABSENT)`, nothing else mutates, no `weld_join` call, the weld sputters. The cost is the six seconds; the world witness is the empty bay footprint at the lane node (LY-20), reachable within one walk.
973	- **E-16. If the weld is attempted onto a vacuum, frozen or dead section**: the weld is allowed and moves nothing (fresh seam: hatch area 0, valves closed, breaker open). The closed hatch creaks (`SEAL_STRAIN`) or frosts at the rim; the player decides when to open it. The weld is never refused for a hazard, only for structure (P1: the hazard is told by the hatch, not the prompt).
974	- **E-17. If `docked` stops holding during the 360-tick channel**: with Web Map & Transit's hold (ASK T1) this cannot happen. Without it, the handoff pre-check (site 2) re-tests `docked` and writes `REJECTED(NOT_DOCKED)` with the sputter, costing the six seconds. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the camera-cut fallback is deleted, Body's request accepted; the offer never drops the `docked` term.)* In the residual window between the site-2 re-test and the apply, a loss of `docked` still lets the weld apply (site 3 reads no pose) and the absorbed hull jumps by `delta_abs` in the exterior layer; Transit's hold (WM-22) makes that window unreachable, and the camera cut does not hide it (BDY-27). Site 3 deliberately does not re-test `docked` (BDY-27: weld legality takes no pose input).
975	- **E-18. If the target section is dormant (`SECTION_NOT_LOADED`)**: the prompt may still show (the offer reads no join structure) and begin is rejected with the standard rejection cue; no channel opens and no time is spent. Dormancy is a section flag, not module-body state, so it is IMMEDIATE.
976	- **E-19. If a weld is attempted while the seat carries a module**: no weld prompt exists (the carry lockout, PC-7 / IA-28, is Interaction's selector) and a forced `begin_weld` is `BUSY`. The player puts the module down or installs it; a torch needs two hands.
977	- **E-20. If the seam hatch is opened during a cancelled-and-resumed cut**: the ledger keeps the progress, but the mode is re-derived at completion, so the resumed cut is RAGGED (D.6). The open leaf and the draught are the witness; the player who wants a clean cut closes the hatch first.
978	- **E-21. If a RAGGED cut applies**: the Graph creates `A_CUT` 24 holes on both sides (including the home side), hull stubs `hp` 2500 and `open_end` ports; `sync_section` must create `stubs[]` entries for every uncapped `open_end` or the O2-lane port hiss could never be capped *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, which would break P2 fairness (ASK I1(vii)). The cut is EXOGENOUS and player-caused, so it is exempt from `W_MIN_WARNING_S`; its tell was the world witnesses before the press. A 20-tile keep-side room falls to the DECOMP band in 382 steps (38 s) and to VACUUM in 960 steps (96 s) (LS-16, D.1) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Capping a stub (V8's follow-up `begin_cap`, M12) stops that port's hiss only; it does not touch the hull hole. The hull hole has no subject in the MVP, so the player's answers are to leave and shut the door behind them (a closed OPENING isolates the room and the rest of the ship stops venting) or to accept the loss of the room until Vertical Slice content closes the hole.
979	- **E-22 `[VS-B]` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. If a keep-side cut leaves a crewmate on the leaving piece**: they are stranded on the detached body, which drifts without rotation. Counterplay (MSA-18): the 4 s lit, loud channel is the tell, and a crewmate who opens the hatch from the far side and stands in the passage before completion makes the cut `MSA.CUT_BLOCKED` (AC-MSA-123); a crewmate who only opens the hatch makes the cut RAGGED. If no one is in the passage the cut proceeds and there is no blanket far-side gate in MVP and Vertical Slice A (Q4: "death is a bitch; it happens"; in solo play a gate is vacuous). Recovery is Web Map & Transit's (ASK T1, ASK T2). Vertical Slice B gates it as `CUT_STRANDS` by default (user ruling D53): a keep-side cut with another seat in the leaving component is rejected `MSA.CUT_STRANDS` at handoff and completion unless the cutter's `harm_eligible` bit is set (MSA-18, Open Question 2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
980	- **E-53. If derelict B is welded into the home body** *(added after E-52 and kept last in this group; id kept stable for AC-MSA-122)*: the Graph's section record keeps `kind` DERELICT and so `rate_pm` 2000 (LS-17, LS-25: the rate is keyed on `kind`, and `weld_join`, LS-15, writes no section field). Endogenous wear and overload on B's nodes and edges therefore run at twice the home-ship rate after the weld. Every endogenous transition still passes the `W_MIN_WARNING_S` gate, so the tell is kept. Assembly writes no section field and adds no rule (MSA-2). Whether a graft keeps derelict compression is the Graph's call (ASK G7). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **G7 is closed and 2x graft wear is confirmed as intended.** Graph LS-15 and LS-17 state that a welded section keeps its `kind` and `rate_pm` and that "a cut restores nothing"; Assembly keeps that: the graft is the ship's weak point, which is the motive to shed a worn graft (Player Fantasy, the cut anchor). **Observable in a session:** the Graph's own D.15 table gives, for a DERELICT section at `rate_pm` 2000, FUEL-DRIP at 5.3 minutes and HULL-FATIGUE at 6.2 minutes (against 10.5 and 12.5 at home), so an endogenous event on a grafted section is observable well inside a 30 to 60 minute session; AC-MSA-132 asserts the ratio on the Graph's fixtures.)*
981	
982	- **E-54. If the welder is swapped for another tool, or the seat is staggered or DOWNED, during a weld or cut channel** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; new)*: staggering and DOWNED end the channel with abort cause `BODY` (IA-15 lists "stagger, downed, body transfer, seat rebind" under `BODY`) and Interaction credits any finished blocks to the ledger; a tool swap makes `weld_offer` or `seam_cut_offer` false, so IA-14 row 6 aborts the channel with `NOT_ELIGIBLE` within `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS` 6 ticks (the `eligible` re-test of ASK I1(viii), answered). If neither fires before DONE (the swap lands in the last block), the handoff pre-check (site 2) finds `NO_TOOL` and writes `REJECTED(NO_TOOL)` with the family cue and submits nothing. A DOWNED seat never reaches DONE. No `pending`, no mutation. AC-MSA-135.
983	- **E-55 `[VS-B]`. If a seat disconnects or is unbound while its `pending` is set** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; new)*: the SYSTEM completion is already in the kernel queue and is a fact of the world, not of the seat, so it applies as normal if it is still valid (the actor field names the PlayerId that began it; Body's actor for that seat may be despawned, in which case BM3 transfers the remaining actors and the welder is not among them); the seat's record in `assembly.state` is removed with the seat after the TTL resolves, and `last_result` is dropped with it (nobody presents it). A seat that is rebound to a new peer keeps the PlayerId (never the transport peer id, MSA-4), so its `pending` and the cue gate continue. No fault, no orphan record. AC-MSA-136.
984	- **E-56. If the welder stands on the derelict side (the absorbed body) when the weld applies** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; new)*: the welder is on B for the channel (either socket may be focused, MSA-11). The channel record is already consumed at DONE and the Controller's `channel_ref` cleared (IA-14 row 9) before the completion applies, so BM3 transferring the welder to the surviving body is not an abort (E-12 is the case of a crewmate whose own channel is still running); the welder's `abs` is conserved and, with `docked` holding, nothing moves on screen; if the Pipeline's `BODY_TRANSFER` camera cut fires (fallback only) it is hidden by the DONE bar's 12-tick hold. `last_result = DONE` is written for the welder's seat as usual. AC-MSA-137.
985	- **E-57. If a cut detaches the pod, or sections that hold loose items** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; new)*: **the pod cannot be detached by a cut**: it is its own persistent Layout body (WM-5), is never welded, and a cut splits only the welded component into two (LY-14, forest). **Items and fixtures in the leaving component stay in their section records** and travel with the piece (section-local positions are unchanged); the piece becomes a dormant orphan (WM-23) and its contents are unreachable in MVP but are neither destroyed nor duplicated (conservation, AC-MSA-111), and carried items stay with their carrier. The extraction line (strip by V8 salvage before the cut) is how a player keeps what the piece holds. The piece with an avatar on it is the keep-side rule's job to prevent (MSA-18). AC-MSA-138.
986	
987	### Degenerate strategies
988	
989	- **E-23. If the player cancels and restarts a channel repeatedly to "peek" at whether it would work**: the offer is state-independent for module-body state, so the peek reveals nothing; each start costs TOOL noise per accrued tick, up to `B - 1` = 5 ticks of each cancelled block are wasted (D.7), and the ledger lets the work resume only inside `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` 600. There is no free information and no free progress.
990	- **E-24. If the player welds, strips derelict B by V8 salvage, then cuts it away**: this is an intended healthy line (the "extraction" fantasy). Each salvage costs noise and leaves open ends to cap (Interaction's), each module is salvage-once (IDB-17), the cut is `LOUD`, and nothing is minted (conservation).
991	- **E-25. If the player tries to weld, cut and weld again to reset a damaged seam or farm a section**: the second weld returns `SOCKET_NOT_FREE` with no prompt; sockets go `FREE -> WELDED -> CAPPED | CUT_OPEN` and never back (LY-13). The playtest gate must not require a second weld (AC-MSA-41).
992	- **E-26. If the player cuts a section holding a hostile "to kill it"**: a RAGGED cut breaches both sides including the home side, so it is self-harm; there is no force or knockback (BDY-28). A cut removes only a threat the player is leaving behind. Shedding an infested section after the seam has been prepared is healthy P5 play, and a cut made under attack is RAGGED and breaches home, so it is not an escape *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: "escape" removed, the cut is a prepared amputation)*, with the Attention owner's rule that a cut moves the locus and does not reset the meter (ASK A1).
993	- **E-27. If the player stands on the derelict side of a welded seam with the cutter**: no cut prompt exists, because the seat's foot-origin section is not in the component that keeps its body (`seam_cut_offer`, D.2). The self-strand trap (alone on a drifting, sealed body with no free socket and no recovery path in MVP) is unreachable from a prompt; a forced `begin_seam_cut` is rejected `NOT_ELIGIBLE`.
994	- **E-28. If the player presses the install prompt repeatedly on a bay**: each press on an occupied slot resolves `BLOCKED(SLOT_OCCUPIED)` with no time cost, so a row of bays can be scanned by pressing. The residual one-bit oracle is accepted (Q6: no lockout; the carry to the bay is already the price; revisit at playtest, Open Questions). The opposite direction (a bay that looks occupied but is empty) installs the module irreversibly, so the probe is asymmetric but not a faucet.
995	
996	### Save, restore, pause and faults
997	
998	- **E-29. If a restore (load) happens mid-channel**: `interaction.state.post_restore` drops the channel (abort cause `RESTORE`); `assembly.state` has nothing to clear, because the stored `pending` is NONE (MSA-4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; `last_result` is runtime-only and so is empty by construction *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; no orphan `pending`, no cue, no half-bead. The world is as of the save.
999	- **E-30. If a snapshot is taken while `pending` is set** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: that window is not one tick. It runs from the handoff (P3 of `T`, `submit_T`) to the apply (P2 of `T+1`, up to `T+8` under queue truncation) or, when the completion is rejected or dropped, to `submit_T + PENDING_TTL_TICKS + 1` = 13 ticks (E-33). The live `pending` is set while the channel record is already consumed, and the target may already be `WELDED` if a rival completion applied first (INV-10 accepts both on live state, T7); the snapshot stores `pending` as NONE and holds no queued completion, so the restore loses the weld or cut, no weld happened, and the player redoes the six seconds. Restore-then-continue is equal to uninterrupted play wherever MSA-38 says it is (no open ASSEMBLY channel record and no `pending`); the window is the **declared non-snapshot ticks** of MSA-4 (the one asserted difference, PD-1, is a dropped channel record, E-29), asserted explicitly by AC-MSA-61, and **AC-MSA-129 saves at every tick of the window and requires a clean restore** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. ASK S1(a) (`pending_any()`) closes it.
1000	- **E-31. If an autosave comes due during a self-inflicted RAGGED decompression**: it is not written *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier "it may be written" is superseded by the withhold plus soft-gate rule)*. SL-5's soft row (a) counts only ENDOGENOUS descriptors and a RAGGED cut's stubs are EXOGENOUS (LS-16), so the Graph never defers it; the rule is Assembly's `ragged_breach_open()` (the keep-side cut room still venting - hull hole open and `band_p` not VACUUM - or a keep-side port uncapped within `RAGGED_WITHHOLD_MAX_TICKS` 2400 of `cut_at_T`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, which Save/Load treats as a soft-gate row for the interval save (SL-5 soft row (d)) and as a withhold in `event_due` for the event save (MSA-33, D.9, ASK S1(b)); the hard DOWNED/DEAD gate also applies. A Save & Quit inside the window is written RISKY (cause `ASSEMBLY_BREACH`). After the window the next save is taken normally. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* Listed exposure bound: a keep-side room open to a larger connected volume can keep the read true past `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 7200 (V_total 120: 34 542 ticks); the interval save then fires RISKY with cause `ASSEMBLY_BREACH` (SL-5 row (d)); the event save stays latched until the room has vented. This is the intended price of venting the ship, not a defect.
1001	- **E-32. If the game is paused between the DONE tick and the apply**: nothing advances (no P2, no P3, no hook submits; queued commands wait for the first RUNNING tick, CR-16), the TTL and the ledger are in ticks and stop; resume continues as if there had been no pause.
1002	- **E-33. If the completion is rejected at admission (`QUEUE_FULL`) or in P2** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `pending` stays set (and the INV-10 assertion of the debug build stays silent, because the target is allowed to be `WELDED` or `CUT` in this window, T7), no mutation happened, and `assembly.step` writes `NOT_TAKEN` at `submit_T + PENDING_TTL_TICKS + 1`, 13 ticks after submission (superseding the "NOT_TAKEN at T+1" of the earlier proposals); the player gets the family's cue, the world is unchanged and they re-hold E. The queue depth is far above any MVP traffic, so this is a defence.
1003	- **E-34. If a completion is held in the queue for k ticks, 1 <= k <= 8 (per-tick truncation)**: `pending` stays until the apply clears it; `DONE` is written exactly once and `NOT_TAKEN` never, because the kernel's `STALE` bound and the TTL coincide (D.11).
1004	- **E-35. If a mutator called by an Assembly `apply` returns a `FAULT_CODE`, a release postcondition fails (`MSA_SHIFT_DRIFT`, `MSA_VERDICT_DRIFT`), or the release verifier reports INV-1, INV-2, INV-4, INV-5 or INV-7 after an apply** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: GDScript has no throw, so the old wording "makes an apply throw" is withdrawn (MSA-31); the apply calls `ctx.fault(code, detail)` (kernel CR-19) on the first non-`OK` status and returns `ctx.complete()`, and the kernel moves to FAULTED, the faulting command is `Faulted(code)`, the rest of the queue drops with `Dropped(FAULTED)`, no autosave is written over an existing save, and the only exit is a player-initiated restore of the last autosave; the loss window (`fault_loss_ticks`) is about 5400 ticks (1.5 minutes) on average, at most 10800 (3 minutes) when no soft gate defers the interval save, and at most 18000 (5 minutes) at the ceiling (`AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` + `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS`, D.16; "typical" relabelled mean and maximum). This is not Save/Load's death rule (SL-7).
1005	- **E-36. If a restore loads a save in which `welds[]` has an `ACTIVE` row but the Graph has no matching SeamRecord**: INV-1 fails in `assembly.state`'s `post_restore`, the kernel goes LOADING -> FAULTED naming `assembly.state` and INV-1; the save file is untouched; the game never plays on the inconsistent world.
1006	
1007	### Hallucination interplay (MVP class (b); classes (a), (c), (d) are Vertical Slice and the rules are written now)
1008	
1009	- **E-37. If the seam valve renders CLOSED while it is truly OPEN**: the cut is RAGGED, because the mode is derived from true positions. **Under the MSA-23 fallback this render cannot happen at the seam**: the seam's own valve and breaker sprites are TRUTH and the Filter may not wrap them until the Graph and Failure & Trail confirm a zero-gradient lane witness; the case stays specified so the derivation is proven independent of perception (a Perception stub that wraps the sprite anyway, AC-MSA-104, is a Filter defect caught by AC-MSA-126). Once the fallback lifts, the lie is falsifiable beforehand by the witness at the lane (the hiss under a gradient, the zero-gradient lane witness the owners confirmed); a player who looked got a clean cut or a decision, and one who did not took a breach that had a witness (MSA-23).
1010	- **E-38. If the hardpoint renders EMPTY while a module is seated**: the install prompt still appears, because it depends only on what the player carries; the press resolves `BLOCKED(SLOT_OCCUPIED)` with the install bump and the module stays in the hands. The bay's footprint (truth channel) shows the occupant on a closer look. The cost is a walk at carry gait, not a free oracle.
1011	- **E-39. If the hardpoint renders OCCUPIED while it is truly empty**: the prompt appears, the install succeeds and the module is consumed in a bay the player meant to avoid (irreversible: no `remove_module`). Falsify beforehand with the bay footprint.
1012	- **E-40. If a hallucinated "welded" seam is drawn over a socket pair that is truly `FREE`** (Perception Filter, VS): the weld offer and every verdict read true Layout state, the geometry of the real seam is never wrapped, and the prompt `E . Weld` appearing over a "welded" seam is itself the contradiction that falsifies the lie. The Filter may not suppress or fake the prompt (ASK F1).
1013	- **E-41. If a crewmate in the hatch renders as a horror (class (c), VS-B)**: `CUT_BLOCKED` reads true actor presence, not perceived identity, so a deluded player cannot seal a crewmate into a cap; the kept oracle costs one attempt and no time and the Filter must never wrap it.
1014	- **E-42. If the module the player carried home is a phantom (class (d), VS-A)**: the install offer is computed from the true carried def, so no prompt appears at a bay it does not fit; the trip home is one fallback reveal and the cheaper field checks are other owners'.
1015	
1016	### Co-op, MIRROR, zoom and engine-facing cases
1017	
1018	- **E-43 `[VS-B]` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. If a MIRROR client joins while a `last_result` is pending presentation**: `last_result` arrives through `SHARED_SUMMARY`; the presenter acts only if `last_result[p]` is not empty, `(PlayerId, last_result.T)` differs from its `last_seen` (initialised to the value found at the join) and the result lies within `OUTCOME_CUE_WINDOW_TICKS` 60 of now (D.17), so a join never replays a stale cue *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. `assembly.step` does not run on a MIRROR (no authoritative tick); the crewmate's weld in progress is visible through Interaction's replicated channel record (the human channel, P1).
1019	- **E-44 `[VS-B]` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. If a crewmate stands in the hatch to veto a cut (griefing, VS-B)**: the cut is rejected `CUT_BLOCKED` and nothing else happens; the cost to the griefer is standing in a doorway. Recorded for Vertical Slice B; the ship never closes a seam on anyone.
1020	- **E-45. If the player zooms in or out on the integer ladder during a channel**: nothing in the rules depends on zoom; the in-world cursor and bead scale with the world viewport, the prompt plate and linear bar keep their HUD pixel size, offsets stay on the 24-px grid and `abs` is unchanged (R28). Tests run at `k` = 1 and `k_auto + 2` (AC-MSA-64).
1021	- **E-46. If several ticks run in one render frame (catch-up, `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` 4) across a weld** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (the cap is only true if the tick-driver ADR and the boot assertion of T13 hold, AC-MSA-141): the apply runs in its own tick; the P5 subscribers (PROJECTOR, Emitter, Lighting, Trail) coalesce to the latest committed state and never replay each tick's change, so the weld frame costs one rebuild.
1022	- **E-47. If the weld happens on a moving body (`vel` up to `VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK` 16)**: `docked` is relative (equal velocity and the offset), BM3 conserves each actor's `abs`, the survivor's velocity is unchanged and no force is applied (BDY-28). Moving bodies are exercised only by the spike (AC-MSA-72); MVP play welds a docked pair.
1023	- **E-48. If a weld is followed later by a cut of the same seam**: `pos_curr` is not restored to its pre-weld value (the cut subtracts `frame_shift_px` and zeroes the sub-pixel part); `abs` and section-local position are conserved, which is what tests assert (BDY-23).
1024	- **E-49. If `sync_section` returns with `IA_SUBJECT_OVERFLOW` counted on the weld tick**: the weld stays applied (the call is total and fails dark by design); the defect counter rises and the content lint is the fix. For a seam door this reads as a hallucinated dead door, which is why the lint, not the runtime, is the defence (MSA-16, D.14).
1025	- **E-50. If `assembly.step` and `interaction.step` are registered in the wrong order or one is unknown**: boot fails (CR-3: an unknown hook id or a cycle) rather than reading the DONE handoff a tick late; the `after` edge is covered by a test and printable by the Debug Overlay.
1026	- **E-51. If a glowstick (Chemlight) lights the socket instead of the lamp**: whether it satisfies `lit` for the channel is the Lighting and Interaction owners' rule; if it does, the weld proceeds with the lamp pointed elsewhere, a legitimate "weld by glowstick" line that needs no Assembly special case. The sparks are non-emissive and never the light source.
1027	- **E-52. If the detached piece after a cut holds no actor**: it persists as an orphan Layout body with a Body pose row (Body BDY-4); Assembly neither unloads nor discards it (Web Map & Transit's, MSA-24). It counts toward `MAX_BODIES`, which is why D.8 includes it.

The user ruled "I agree with all of your recommendations on those decisions" and, on the held list, "yes to all". 51:Persistence has no fantasy of its own. The promise comes from Pillar 5 — "losing the home-ship or a crewmate costs ship and body, never knowledge" — and from the user's binding rule for death: "This is like project zomboid, death is a bitch. It happens." The emotion this system must produce is that the player believes, without ever checking, that (1) the ship they welded is still there tomorrow exactly as they left it, (2) a death will cost them the minutes since the last autosave and nothing else, and (3) the game never records a moment it could have warned them about: it will not save while a crewmate is down, for ten seconds after one gets up, while a suit is in a critical state, while a warning the world owes them is still open, while a breach they cut is still venting, or (if Attention publishes it) during a breach phase (SL-5); and if a death follows a restore within ten seconds, the restore steps back past that save, unless it is the player's own Save & Quit made without a critical suit (SL-8, R15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R15; cross-GDD fix)*. It does **not** promise to refuse every doomed moment: a death that arrives with no tell and gives the player more than ten seconds after the restore is the world's, not the save's (user ruling, OQ-40). They never feel *saved*; they feel *committed*. Death and quitting never buy back more than the minutes since the last autosave. *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIG
63:| wakes into a moment the game had already warned about *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | the autosave gate defers while any seat is `DOWNED` or `DEAD`, for `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks after a recovery, while a seat is `CRITICAL`, while a Life-Support Graph warning window or a self-inflicted breach is still open, and (if Attention publishes it) outside a calm breach phase (SL-5); a death that follows a restore within `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks steps back past it (SL-8; a `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` excepted, R15 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R15)*); what the gate cannot see beyond that is not promised *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | a death that was warned about was theirs to avoid; one that came with no tell is the world's, not the save's |

173:| `risky_cause` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | string[] | The closed set of soft inputs that were true at the write: `GRAPH_TELL`, `ATTENTION_TELL`, `BREACH_PHASE`, `SEAT_STATE`, `VITALS`, `ASSEMBLY_BREACH`; empty exactly when `risky` is false. A member outside the set, or a non-empty list with `risky` false, is refused (`SL_PRECHECK_HEADER_FIELD_TYPE`). SL-8 reads it: a `QUIT` generation keeps the RISKY-window step-back only when `VITALS` is in it |
201:When a due save has waited `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` and only **soft** conditions are closed, it is written anyway and its header is tagged `RISKY`, with `risky_cause` listing every soft input that was true *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. A hard condition is never overridden: a `DOWNED` or `DEAD` world is never written by an autosave or by a Save & Quit (SL-6), and the refractory is never shortened by the cap. *(Orchestrator ruling: R4 says the cap "writes anyway"; read literally that would record the very trap the gate exists to avoid, and would write a state the death stub is about to discard. Three specialists proposed three splits; the ruling is that DOWNED and DEAD are hard, the cap overrides soft conditions only, and the derived loss ceiling in Formulas holds. `GATE_SOFT_STATES` is a systems-designer refinement: a restore drops channel progress and turns `STAGGERED` into `IDLE` (PC-17), and a mid-transit state is Web Map's to restore.)* **Consequence stated plainly:** in the solo MVP a downed seat dies after `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` 1 800 (or sooner on a `give_up`), well before the cap, so a `RISKY` generation is reachable through chained Graph warning windows held past the cap, a `CRITICAL` suit or an open self-inflicted breach held past the cap, the Attention view, or a transit/channel state held past the cap or at a Save & Quit (SL-6); none of them involves a downed seat. The step-back of SL-8 is no longer near-dead code *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulin
203:**SL-6 — Save & Quit.** From the pause panel: `request_snapshot` while `PAUSED` (`PAUSED → SAVING → PAUSED`, `T` unchanged), write a generation of kind `QUIT`, and `request_shutdown` only after the write verifies (`WRITTEN`). The call is host-local (CR-15) and is never named a command in the MVP. Quitting is **never deferred** and bypasses the **soft** gate conditions only: if a soft condition was closed at request time the generation is written immediately and tagged `RISKY` (alternatives rejected: refusing to quit traps the player; quitting without writing silently throws away up to one interval). 1598	*Ids AC-MSA-01 to AC-MSA-128 keep the pre-assigned meaning of the criterion index (T8) (AC-MSA-46 and AC-MSA-66 are absorbed into AC-MSA-01 and AC-MSA-58; split ids carry letters); the ids that the corrections and the Edge Cases added continue from AC-MSA-73 (AC-MSA-122 covers E-53; AC-MSA-123 to AC-MSA-128 were added by later revisions); ids 113 to 115 and 119, which the QA review had reserved, are reassigned to the Game Feel benchmarks. Every criterion carries a tag and a rule or edge-case reference. **Tags:** `(auto)` an automated test in `tests/unit/modular_ship_assembly/` or `tests/integration/modular_ship_assembly/`; `(lint)` a static scan or data lint; `(review)` a design or code review; `(manual)` a playtest or a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`; `(spike)` only the throwaway spike (see Spike Plan) can answer it. **Status markers:** `(depends: ASK Gn / CONFLICT Cn)` means the criterion rests on a provisional ask or an open conflict in the Dependencies tables (T14, T15); a failure there means "contract not yet agreed", not necessarily a defect. `[VS]` marks a Vertical Slice criterion whose rule is specified now. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **`[VS-B]` marks a co-op criterion (it needs a second seat, a MIRROR client or a crewmate) and is excluded from the MVP gate**; where a rule has a double-based form that is single-player (for example `CUT_BLOCKED` with a Body double, AC-MSA-36), that form gates the MVP and says so. Ids AC-MSA-129 to AC-MSA-148 are added by the first design review; AC-MSA-05 is split into 05a and 05b.)**
1599	
1600	**Gate levels** (`.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`): Logic and Integration are BLOCKING; Visual/Feel and UI are BLOCKING and need a **retained** screenshot (a captured-and-discarded one is an assertion, not evidence); Config/Data is ADVISORY. Story typing: weld, cut, install and the verifier are Integration stories (several owners' mutators in one apply); D.1, D.6 to D.11, D.17 and D.18 are Logic; the knob and data lints are Config/Data; AC-MSA-68, 71, 113 and 114 are Visual/Feel plus UI.
1601	
1602	**Test rules.** Deterministic (no wall clock, no unseeded RNG, a fixed `world_seed`); isolated; assertions on `abs(actor)` and section-local position, never raw `pos_curr`; fixtures from constant files or factory functions; the doubles are a SYSTEM-origin submitter (tests cannot reach `weld` or `seam_cut` any other way), an Interaction double (except where a criterion says it needs the real one), a Body double with `docked` controllable, a Perception stub, and a Graph double for capacity. **Performance criteria are gated on the named reference machines** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*: RM-DESKTOP (minimum-spec desktop: Windows 10/11 64-bit, 6-core/6-thread CPU of the Intel Core i5-9400F / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 class, 8 GB RAM, GPU of the GTX 1050 Ti 4 GB / RX 570 4 GB class, SATA SSD, 1920x1080 at 60 Hz, P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 16.6 ms) and RM-DECK (Steam Deck LCD 2022, SteamOS stable, 1280x800 at 60 Hz panel, 30 fps target, P99 ceiling 33.3 ms), recorded in `project.yaml` `qa.min_spec`; the build type for every wall-clock figure is a release export (Godot 4.7.2 release export template, not the editor and not a debug template), renderer `forward_plus`, vsync on, a 120-frame warm-up, with the startup read-back (renderer, driver) recorded with each result; a pass needs P99 <= 90 % of the machine's ceiling; the developer's machine is not a reference machine and its figures are indicative only; the measurement protocol is that release export build, 300 warm-up ticks discarded for the apply budgets, then the stated sample; apply budgets with headless render off, frame-time budgets with render on. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **the performance criteria (AC-MSA-17b, 23, 62, 63, 108) stay gating**: the machines and build type are now named (R12, above), so a criterion is pending spike measurement on RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK, not blocked, and the spike records the measured value as an input. A criterion marked `(spike)` produces a number for the spike report as a design input; the **story evidence** is the same assertion as an automated test under `tests/performance/modular_ship_assembly/` or `tests/unit/` run in the nightly job, never the throwaway spike report. The budgets themselves are re-derived from the S0 GDScript micro-benchmark before they are judged (D.15).)*

Each `(lint)` criterion names its rule: LINT-MSA-03 (AC-MSA-03: the only block written is `assembly.state`), LINT-MSA-06 (AC-MSA-06: no packed-array field), LINT-MSA-09 (AC-MSA-09: completion payload fields, `max_age_ticks`, TTL range), LINT-MSA-10 (AC-MSA-10: no second definition of the predicate; the equivalence itself is a unit test), LINT-MSA-13 (AC-MSA-13: no full `can_join`, `check_install_module` or node-state accessor in a PLAYER-origin `validate`), LINT-MSA-17 (AC-MSA-17a: `weld_offer` source), LINT-MSA-20 (AC-MSA-20 and 58: forbidden identifiers), LINT-MSA-30 (AC-MSA-30: calls Assembly never makes), LINT-MSA-47 (AC-MSA-47: no `push_stimulus`), LINT-MSA-57 (AC-MSA-57: no `PERCEPTION_OUT` reference), LINT-MSA-119 (AC-MSA-119: no shake, hit-stop, rumble or time-scale). It writes no block, ever; it owns only local state (raw aim, last-acknowledged intents, hold timers, run latch, active device, context, pre-play tokens, menu latch and last NAV direction). It samples input for gameplay intents **in the physics callback imme

1275	
1276	1. **World changes are cuts.** Bead, cap plate, ragged piece, jambs and leaf, scar and the fresh-to-old swap appear by a cut on a committed tick. No tween, scale, fade, dissolve or draw-on. The change lands on the P5 frame of the apply; catch-up ticks (`MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` 4) coalesce to the latest state and are never replayed per tick (MSA-39).
1277	2. **Work loop**: six frames, two-handed, tool forward, stiff-weighted (ART 5.2); the same loop, speed and spark cadence for every target and every outcome (duration and cadence depend on the channel, never the target, IA-11c). No squash, smear, overshoot or recoil on abort, completion or any outcome cue.
1278	3. **Facing lock** during a channel; five drawn facings, three mirrored (the tool hand swaps, ART 5 consistency note 8).
1279	4. **Chest-point lint** (ART 5.1, IA art lint): in work, carry and install frames no tool, limb, module or effect covers `anchor_chest_<facing>` or the beam's forward arc. Sparks anchor at `anchor_hand_<facing>`.
1280	5. **Luminance**: nothing on the HUD above 3 Hz (HR-13). World sparks and outcome transients: at most 3 luminance transitions per second. No full-frame flash, ever. Positional stepping is exempt (accessibility-specialist to confirm, as IA already asks).
1281	6. **Camera**: a weld or cut that changes the avatar's body is PIPE's `BODY_TRANSFER` hard cut, never a pan. A docked weld shows no visible `delta_abs`. The detached piece translates without rotation. Assembly adds no shake, impulse or screen effect (BDY-28, `JOLT_PX` 0).

1310	**Sanity palette (ART 4.4, Corollary).** No violet (`#8A3FD1`, `#B07BE6`) and no flesh (`#D9A58C`, `#B5705C`) anywhere in Assembly's presentation, with no exception: the violet gleam and fringe are the Perception Filter's, outside the sprite, on corruptible readings only. The cursor, plate, bar, bead, cap plate, ragged piece, sparks, outcome transients and seat frames are all in the sane palette.
1311	
1312	| Element | Colour | Notes |
1313	|---|---|---|
1314	| Bead (fresh and old); bolt rhythm and edge bead of the cap plate | Hull Grey `#8C949C` | thin element only, never a plane (4.1). Fresh is brighter and cleaner, old is dulled and scuffed; at least one value step between them |
1315	| Cap plate body, jambs, ragged-piece body | Graphite lit `#5C6670` / Graphite mid `#2A303A` | Hull Grey is never a plane. Kerf is Graphite mid; scorch is Void Steel `#0B1018`; all matte, hue-less |
1316	| Weep | O2 Cyan `#3FD6E8` (mist) | FT's, soft drifting. With Power Amber, the only lane hue at the MVP seam |
1317	| Rim frost | Coolant Ice `#C8E6F5` | FT row 26 under a thermal gradient |
1318	| Lane pipes at birth | Graphite lit, no emission | ART 4.2 "dead loop"; they take their hue only when carrying (POWER lane Power Amber `#F2C230`, O2 lane O2 Cyan) |
1319	| Sparks | Tungsten family: core `#FFE2A8`, body `#FFCC66`, hue at least 38 degrees | never Fuel Ember, Power Amber or Alarm Red; non-emissive |
1320	| Socket cursor | Tungsten fixture `#FFCC66` (UI accent), flat, unlit, non-emissive | not a light, so no exposure and no beam shape; geometry is the primary channel (HR-11) |
1321	| Plate, bar, needle-mark, keycap | IA's palette unchanged: Ground `#1C2128`, border Graphite lit, Paper White `#DDE4EA`, fill Tungsten `#FFCC66` | no loop hue, no Alarm Red |
1322	| Carried module; seat dust | the module's own palette; dust is Graphite mid | |
1323	
1324	**Never on any Assembly element:** Alarm Red (a RAGGED breach's sweep belongs to the Graph, FT and the alarm owner); Chemlight `#86B896` (light colour only); the loop hues on the cursor, plate, bar or outcome cues (a hue is a sentence about a system); any new hue (so no new ART 4.7 entry is required).
1325	
1326	**Required tests before approval (ART 8.9).**
1327	1. **ART 4.4 sampling test on the fresh bead first.** A fresh bead under chest-lamp Tungsten is the documented near-case (Hull Grey under fixture Tungsten computes to about hue 43, S 56 %, V 55 %). Sample `seam_straight_fresh` and the cap plate's Hull Grey bolts under all four beam shapes; hue must stay at least 36 degrees. "Brighter and cleaner" means higher value, never higher saturation or an orange pull; if drift appears, pull toward yellow, never desaturate the light.
1328	2. **Greyscale pass (4.5).** Bead Hull Grey (L* about 61) against Graphite lit (about 43) is an 18-point gap and must survive achromatopsia; the weep (about 79) against the bead must also separate by motion (drifting mist versus a static raised bead).
1329	3. **25 % silhouette test (3.1)** on the seam in a lit frame: the bead reads as a line with a break at the hatch.
1330	4. **Colourblind (4.7):** at the MVP seam there is no Coolant and no Fuel lane, so Hull Grey against Fuel Ember (L* 61 against 61) cannot occur until a Vertical Slice lane is added; the backup (raised seam versus glossy puddle) is already named. Bowed rim versus rim frost differ in shape; sputter, gutter and bump differ in shape.
1331	
1332	### Truth channel versus corruptible
1333	
1334	TRUTH means the consequence channel or an anchor, drawn identically on every client and never wrapped by the Perception Filter. CORRUPTIBLE means module-body presentation that a class (b) hallucination may draw wrongly, always with the palette leak.
1335	
1336	| Visual | Class | Reason |
1337	|---|---|---|
1338	| Seam bead (fresh and old), floor and wall pieces | **TRUTH** | Layout geometry derived from `welds[]` and `welded_at_T`; the age swap is a derived read (LY-33). The Filter never wraps it (MSA-35, LY-34) |
1339	| Hatch plate, jambs and leaf, **leaf position** | **TRUTH** | Layout and Graph geometry and opening area; whether the seam is open is physical, consequence channel, falsified by walking or by the draught |
1340	| Cap plate, ragged piece, scar, "nothing beyond" | **TRUTH** | Layout socket state `CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN` |

The Perception Filter may not wrap these sprites until the Graph and Failure & Trail confirm a consequence-channel lane witness that exists at zero gradient (ASK G8, ASK FT1). When both confirm in writing, this row reverts to CORRUPTIBLE and the next row's witness carries the load. AC-MSA-126 |

1348	| Lane pipe emission, flow chevrons, dash-pulse | **TRUTH (immune, Perception Filter PF-5 row 17a, TRUTH_PX; registry `truth_channel_union`)** | MSA-23 needs the cut mode predictable from the world alone; the "seam breaker is closed" and "valve is open" witnesses must not rest only on a corruptible lever sprite. a state the pipe does not show (an open valve at zero gradient) is covered by the seam-lane valve and breaker fallback row above, not by this one |

1350	| Any phantom seam, false "welded" state or phantom bead (hallucination classes b and d, VS) | **CORRUPTIBLE, Filter layer only** | Must leak: a violet fringe at its edge, never the raised-bead geometry, no collision, no occlusion, no weep, no hatch subject. It never reaches `welds[]`, the consequence channel or the bead geometry (MSA-35). The check is cheap: walk into it |

1352	Two hard lines. (1) No Assembly cue, cursor or plate is ever recoloured, shaken or glided under any sanity stage (HR-6, HR-13). (2) `CUT_BLOCKED` stays a kept truth oracle (a real person is in the hatch, a phantom is not an actor); the Filter must never draw a crewmate-as-horror out of the hatch rectangle or hide a real one in it.

1361

1363	|---|---|---|---|---|

Plain and quiet: a closed door that is never going to open. Must read at 25 % as a plate where a port was | P |

Solid and light-blocking | P |
1367	| `ui_cursor_socket_corner.png`, `ui_cursor_socket_edge.png` | 2 pieces, 9-slice to `width_tiles` x 48 by 24 | none (flat, unlit) | The VA-2 bracket; `ui_` carries no map suffix (ART 8.5). World-space placement, flat material, non-emissive | P |
