content.content:
1398	## Game Feel
1399	
1400	*Units: 1 tick = 16.7 ms (`TICK_RATE` 60); a render frame at 60 Hz is one tick, at 30 Hz two. Every number is a design target for the presenters, the HUD and the animation budget; the simulation values are the Formulas section's (D.7 for timing, D.9 for the shape-change time, D.17 for the cue gate). No animation frame rate is invented here: ART 5.2 owns the work loop's six frames and Interaction owns the bar's cadence. Assembly's feel is mostly inherited (Interaction's channel feel, the Pipeline's camera cut, Failure and Trail's weep); this section fixes the numbers Assembly adds: two durations, a delay of one tick, three one-shot cues and the discipline of what is not drawn. The Visual/Audio section owns what is drawn; this section owns how long it takes and how it feels to operate.*
1401	
1402	### Feel Reference
1403	
1404	**Borrow:** Project Zomboid's timed contextual actions (a linear bar, cancelled by moving, no skill-check minigame, no hit-stop) for the *channel*, and the hands-free chest lamp of *Pandorum* (the beam stays on the job while both hands work) for the *exposure*. The quality borrowed is deliberate, stationary, stiff competence under a held breath: pressing is instant, the work takes visible time, leaving is always free, and the finished thing is a fact in the room, not a fanfare. For the cut, the borrowed quality is the clean terrible certainty of *Aliens*-style bulkhead sealing: a loud burn-through and a plate where a door was.
1405	
1406	**Anti-references:** (1) a Barotrauma-style repair minigame or any QTE (a UI surface that could leak module-body truth, and a rhythm demand the "I can leave now" test forbids); (2) Space Engineers or Starbase-style welding that **grows geometry with progress** (a drawn bead with no sim state behind it, VA-10, would be exactly that lie); (3) a building-game ghost-placement confirm (the anti-pillar: not a freeform builder); (4) any screen shake, hit-stop or camera punch on the weld or the cut (`JOLT_PX` 0, BDY-28).
1407	
1408	### Input Responsiveness
1409	
1410	| Action | Max input-to-response | Ticks | Notes |
1411	|---|---|---|---|
1412	| Press `interact` on the weld prompt: ACK pre-play | the same render frame | 0 (at most 1 frame) | keycap drop, bar at fill 0, first work pose; the hand never waits for the sim (PCI) |
1413	| `begin_weld` or `begin_seam_cut` applied, CONFIRMED | at most 1 tick after the press | 1 | `queued_tick` is the next tick; the bar then fills from the committed value; Assembly adds no latency of its own (the begin only opens the channel, MSA-3) |
1414	| First TOOL noise push | the first accrued tick | 1 (`e` = 1) | the web may hear this from tick 1 (D.7); no visible change marks it (P3: shown in the world, never a meter) |
1415	| Immediate reject at begin (`BUSY`, `NO_TOOL`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `NOT_LIT`, `NOT_ELIGIBLE`, `CUT_BLOCKED`, a structural Layout or Graph reason) | ack withdrawn within 1 render frame of the result event | 1 to 2 | the standard IA rejection: dull sound, no shake, flash or red; capped by IA's `PREPLAY_MAX_TICKS` 2 (proposed) |
1416	| Let go (release) or `cancel_channel` | the channel ends in the same P2 | 1 | the bar drain is cosmetic and never blocks a new press |
1417	| Move intent during a channel | abort before accrual on that tick | 1 | the body moves at once; the move always wins (PC-7). A cancel wastes at most `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` - 1 = 5 accrued ticks (D.7) |
1418	| Hold `E` to completion, weld | 360 ticks to the DONE handoff (6.0 s); the world changes 1 tick later | `D` + 1 = 361 | `T_apply - Tb` = `D` + 1 for a fresh channel (D.7) |
1419	| Hold `E` to completion, seam cut | 240 ticks to the DONE handoff (4.0 s); the world changes 1 tick later | `D` + 1 = 241 | deliberately faster than the weld (a prepared amputation, not an escape verb; revisit if players use it as a free panic button, which would show as RAGGED cuts under attack in the playtest log) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
1420	| DONE handoff to the visible world change | one tick, 16.7 ms | 1 | the completion is queued in P3 of `T_done` and applies in P2 of `T_apply`; the apply and the P5 batch land in the same render frame, inside the bar's 12-tick DONE hold |
1421	| Weld applied to the first weep | at most one Graph block, 100 ms | at most 6 | the first Graph hook (`graph.propagate.power`, `.atmo` or `.failure`, whichever is due next, within 6 ticks) sees the new seam *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; FT draws the s-trace from that step |
1422	| Failed-completion cue (`REJECTED` at the handoff) | the handoff tick's presenter frame | 0 to 1 | the handoff itself finds the reason, so there is nothing to wait for |
1423	| Failed-completion cue (`NOT_TAKEN`, a dropped completion) | `PENDING_TTL_TICKS` + 1 = 13 ticks after the submission (sim), plus at most `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` 4 ticks to the first rendered frame (AC-MSA-115) | 13 (217 ms) sim, 17 (283 ms) end to end | the one slow cue; it is a defence path that the MVP queue depth never normally reaches (E-33) |
1424	| Install press (TAP) | depress frame at the press; clunk at the Applied result | 1 | a sound cannot be withdrawn, so it waits for the result; an install is one tick (no channel) |
1425	| `BLOCKED` install cue | the Applied result's frame | 1 | the bump is played from `last_result` (D.17), one frame after the result |
1426	
1427	### Animation Feel Targets
1428	
1429	| Animation or cue | Startup | Active | Recovery | Feel goal |
1430	|---|---|---|---|---|
1431	| Weld work loop | first pose held from the press (ACK) until CONFIRMED (at most 1 tick) | six-frame loop for the whole accrued length (360 ticks), **not scrubbed by progress** | **0**: a cut to idle on every terminal state (no recoil, no overshoot) | stiff, committed, readable at 50 % size |
1432	| Cut work loop | as above | six-frame loop for 240 ticks | 0 | the same loop, faster bar (6 versus 9 ticks per px) |
1433	| Bar fill (weld) | appears at 0 on ACK | stepped, **9 ticks per art px** (150 ms) over 40 px | DONE holds 12 ticks then cuts | a clock, not a reading of the job |
1434	| Bar fill (cut) | as above | stepped, **6 ticks per art px** (100 ms) over 40 px | DONE holds 12 ticks then cuts | a clock |
1435	| Cancel drain | 0 | 2x fill speed (IA `CONFIRM_DRAIN_RATE`) | cut by the next ACK | "I let go" |
1436	| Abort | 0 | snap to empty at once | break-notch held 12 ticks | "the world stopped me" |
1437	| Weld result: bead and jambs appear | 0: the P5 frame of the apply | **a cut, no animation** (0 ticks) | the pieces persist | quiet finality: the room changed, nothing celebrated |
1438	| Cut result: cap plate or ragged piece | 0: the P5 frame of the apply | a cut (0 ticks) | persists; the detached section translates without rotation | a clean, terrible certainty |
1439	| Weld non-DONE cue (sputter) | 0 | at most **24 ticks** (400 ms): three irregular spark bursts | 0: ends by a cut, no residue | "the bead did not hold", dull and neutral |
1440	| Cut non-DONE cue (gutter) | 0 | at most **18 ticks** (300 ms): the spark stream thins to nothing | 0 | "the seam held" |
1441	| Install non-DONE cue (bump) | 0 | **6 ticks** the carried module sprite offsets 2 art px toward the bay, **6 ticks** it returns (12 ticks, 200 ms total) | 0 | "it did not seat", positional only, no squash |
1442	| Install DONE (seat) | 0 | the module slides at most 4 art px into the mount over **4 frames**, then still | 0 | cause and rest; weight, then waiting for the rotor |
1443	| Fresh-to-old bead swap | 0 | a cut at `SEAM_OLD_AFTER_TICKS` 36000 (10 min) | 0 | the ship ageing; never noticed in the moment |
1444	
1445	### Impact Moments
1446	
1447	| Impact type | Duration | Effect | Configurable |
1448	|---|---|---|---|
1449	| Hit-stop (freeze frames) | none | not used at all (BDY-28; the weight comes from sound and the 6 s stillness) | no |
1450	| Screen shake | none | not used; `JOLT_PX` 0 and `BODY_DOCK_CONTACT` moves nothing on screen | no (a Pipeline knob; Assembly adds none) |
1451	| Camera move | 1 frame hard cut, only when the avatar's body changes | PIPE's `BODY_TRANSFER` cut; on a docked weld `delta_abs` is zero so nothing visibly jumps; the detached piece translates without rotation | the cut is the Pipeline's |
1452	| Controller rumble | none | not used for the channel; the Adapter owns rumble and gives Assembly no cue | n/a |
1453	| Time-scale slowdown | none | not used | no |
1454	| Weld DONE | 1 tick of world change inside a 12-tick bar hold | the bead settles; the single audible "it is done"; no sting, no flash | audio level only |
1455	| Cut DONE | `LOUD` one-shot one tick before the plate; the plate on the P5 frame | a loud burn-through, then a cap plate or a ragged scar and the Graph's breach for RAGGED | audio mix only |
1456	| First weld (hero beat) | the whole 6 s plus the 1 s after | the 1 s after is quiet but for the bead settling; the first weep hiss and any creak ramp in at its end (ASK FT3) and the bar disappears at the cut *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; a **mixing preference** routed to Adaptive Audio, not a sim rule: no escalation window and no invulnerability is added (P2 already requires its own tell) | Adaptive Audio's |
1457	
1458	### Weight and Responsiveness Profile
1459	
1460	- **Weight**: heavy and deliberate. A weld is six seconds of standing still, lit, with both hands busy; it is the single heaviest verb the player performs at a socket, and the cut (four seconds) is lighter in time but heavier in consequence. The weight comes from stillness and exposure, never from effects.
1461	- **Player control**: high at every moment *before* the DONE handoff (let go or step away at any tick; the cost is at most five wasted ticks and the channel's partial progress is held for `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` 600); **none** in the single tick between the handoff and the apply, by design (one tick, 16.7 ms, the price of an atomic apply).
1462	- **Snap quality**: crisp and binary on the world side. The hatch plate becomes jambs and a bead in one frame; the door becomes a cap plate in one frame; there are no half-states and no transitions. The bar is stepped, never smooth.
1463	- **Acceleration model**: none. The work loop starts at its first pose on the press and stops by a cut; the bar fills at a constant rate; nothing ramps, eases or overshoots.
1464	- **Failure texture**: every failure is dull, short and neutral, and **identical across reasons** (P4): the weld sputters, the flame gutters, the module bumps. There is no red, no text, no shake and no punishment animation. The player learns *why* from the world (the lane node that was salvaged, the module already in the bay, the crewmate in the hatch), not from the cue. A failure after cost (six seconds spent) is the worst case, and it is rare by construction (`PORT_ABSENT`, `SLOT_OCCUPIED`, `NOT_TAKEN`, a hatch entered late); the cost is the time and the exposure, which are the Pillar 3 price, and nothing is lost that cannot be redone.
1465	- **The inert-weld risk (named)**: for six seconds the world does not change (no progressive bead, VA-10), and after the bead appears a weld moves nothing (LS-15). Both are intended (beat 1 then beat 2 of the Player Fantasy) and both are the loudest feel risk in the system. The only legitimate remedies are sim-backed (the leaf and jambs make the hatch look *newly operable*; the creak or frost when a gradient exists; the weep), never a drawn progressive bead, a flourish or an auto-open. Playtested by the targets below; an open question for the playtest gate. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the remedies are now owned, not hoped for: the Beat 1 release (the tool loop ends and the room goes quiet), the starting gradient as a Derelict Authoring requirement with a fixture check (ASK D3, AC-MSA-140), preloaded and warmed-up assets, and a cold-cache, export-build, whole-frame measurement in S3 (MSA-39).)*
1466	
1467	### Feel Acceptance Criteria
1468	
1469	Checked by playtest unless an AC id is given (the measurable ones are in the Acceptance Criteria section). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the playtest items below are scored by the pooled rule of Validation targets, not by "no playtester ever says X": an item passes if at least 17 of 20 pooled judgements (5 players x 4 prompts) go the intended way and the two raters agree on at least 80 % of coded sentences; the word lists are the Validation targets' lists; "floaty", "laggy" and "unresponsive" are counted as coded sentences, not as an absolute ban. These items are tuning inputs, not build gates.)*
1470	
1471	- [ ] The weld reads as heavy and exposed: playtesters volunteer that they felt watched, standing still, and none describes it as "building" (they say "our ship", "I welded that").
1472	- [ ] No playtester asks "did the weld work?" after the bead appears. If they ask during the six seconds, that is acceptable and intended.
1473	- [ ] The bar's fill is within 1 px of the same fraction of the bar's length at 25, 50, 75 and 100 % of `D` (AC-MSA-113).

1482	## UI Requirements
1483	
1484	**Assembly draws no pixel of its own and adds no screen, menu, meter, panel, tooltip or reason text; but it does have real UI *content*, so this section is the contract on what Assembly feeds the surfaces that others draw.** The prompt plate, the linear bar and the carry-drop prompt are Interaction's and the HUD's (HUD & Suit Layer, Designed; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: no longer provisional*); the in-world socket cursor is Layout's socket highlight (Layout presentation data); the outcome cues are drawn by presenters (PRESENTATION subscribers) from one Assembly block. Pillar 1 forbids the screens a ship-building game would have (no blueprint view, no build mode, no placement ghost with rotation, no connection panel, no weld-quality or seam-health bar, no surge number, no "welded" badge, no reason text); the UI of this system is a keycap, a verb word, a bar and the world itself. This is not a "no UI" system: it has an information table, and the HUD GDD must meet it.
1485	
1486	| Information | Display location | Update frequency | Condition |
1487	|---|---|---|---|
1488	| Weld prompt: keycap glyph for `interact` on the current device plus `tr(verb_weld)` | beside the focused `WELD_SOCKET` subject, at `world_to_hud(anchor_o)`, on the HUD layer outside the world SubViewport (Interaction's plate) | once per render frame from `focus_view` | `weld_offer` (D.2) true: welder equipped, lit, in reach, socket `FREE`, `can_attach` passes, `docked` holds. Hidden otherwise, with no "can't weld" state |
1489	| Seam-cut prompt: keycap plus `tr(verb_seam_cut)` | as above, on the seam's hatch frame | as above | `seam_cut_offer` true: cutter equipped, lit, in reach, socket `WELDED` on an `ACTIVE` seam, seat on the keep-side component (MSA-18). Never shown on the derelict side |
1490	| Install prompt: keycap plus `tr(verb_install)` | anchored to the hardpoint's mount; the carry-drop prompt `G . Drop` stays at the foot origin (AD-5 keep-outs) | as above | carrying a def in `compatible_defs(h)`, hardpoint subject focused, reach, lit, not staggered. An incompatible def: nothing |
1491	| Channel bar (LONG class, 40 art px interior) with needle-mark | attached to the plate's long edge on the side facing away from the anchor (Interaction's component) | `fill_px` per committed tick, no interpolation: weld 9 ticks per px, cut 6 ticks per px | the local seat's `channel_view.state` is ACK, CONFIRMED or PROGRESS for an ASSEMBLY-owned channel; terminal frames (drain, snap and notch, DONE hold 12 ticks) are Interaction's |
1492	| In-world socket cursor (four chamfer-corner brackets, Tungsten, flat, non-emissive) | on the focused socket's reference rectangle, in the avatar's body frame, world space | with the prompt, by a cut | exactly the prompt's condition, and only inside the lit area (the honest edge) |
1493	| Outcome cue (sputter, gutter or bump) | at the socket or on the carried module, in the world; **no HUD element** | once per `last_result.T` change (D.17), inside `OUTCOME_CUE_WINDOW_TICKS` 60 | `last_result.outcome` is `REJECTED`, `BLOCKED` or `NOT_TAKEN` for the local seat; one cue per verb family, identical across reasons, never a string or a number |
1494	| Everything else | nothing | never | `q`, `leak_bp`, `hp_seam`, `cap_seam`, `A_seam_m`, the `surge[]` magnitude, seam age, weld count, body count, socket state as text, the cut mode and the reason of any non-DONE outcome are **never displayed** (AC-MSA-19) |
1495	
1496	**What the surfaces read (and nothing else).** The HUD reads `focus_view` and `channel_view` (Interaction's IA-41 views); the presenters read the local seat's `last_result` from `assembly.state` (a SIM block, replicated as `SHARED_SUMMARY`) and `welds[]`-derived geometry from Layout. Neither reads `pending`, any Graph node or edge, `forced_mode`, `served_pm` or any `PERCEPTION_OUT` block. Assembly publishes two pure predicates for the surfaces (`weld_offer` and `seam_cut_offer`, used as the `eligible` of the `begin_*` declaration rows, MSA-12) and the pure read `last_shape_change_T()` for Save/Load; it publishes no other read view *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: except `ragged_breach_open()`, the pure read Save/Load consults to withhold the `ASSEMBLY_CUT` event while the keep-side cut room is venting or a keep-side port is uncapped, MSA-33)*.
1497	
1498	**Rules the HUD and Interaction owners must meet for Assembly's verbs.**
1499	
1500	- *Labels are verbs, not states (IA-11).* `verb_weld`, `verb_seam_cut` and `verb_install` carry no condition word (no "Weld (docked)", "Cut (sealed)", "Install (compatible)"). `verb_seam_cut` must stay distinct from V8's `verb_cut` (module salvage): an ASK to Interaction to add the two tokens, not to reuse `verb_cut`. English proposals, owned by the HUD GDD: "Weld", "Cut away", "Install". Localisation through `tr()` with StringName keys; the plate grows to `PROMPT_PLATE_MAX_W_PX` then wraps, never truncating.
1501	- *The prompt may be late, never wrong.* Hide is immediate (the same render frame the offer goes false: a prompt for a pair that is no longer docked, or a seat that stepped into the dark, is a lie by commission); show may be debounced by the HUD (IA D.UI-2), because a late prompt omits a hint and the verb works as soon as it is focused.
1502	- *Bar semantics.* The bar is the actor's own elapsed time, `fill_px = floor(progress_pm x L / 1000)` with `L` 40 and `progress_pm` from ticks only (IA D.UI-1). It is **identical for SEALED and RAGGED**, for every `q` and for every module-body state (AC-MSA-88); the channel length is the declared `D` and never varies with the target. A resumed channel starts from its credited offset, not from zero (IA ledger).
1503	- *No reason text, anywhere.* A rejected begin uses the standard IA rejection (ack withdrawn, dull sound); a post-channel non-DONE outcome uses the family cue of MSA-34; neither carries a word. Accessibility announcements, when AccessKit is in scope (Alpha), are fixed phrases keyed by outcome *state* (done, did not hold), never by cause.
1504	- *Cursor and plate are meta-register truth.* They are functions of static inputs, never lie-capable, and never recoloured, shaken or glided at any sanity stage (HR-6, HR-13). The Perception Filter must not suppress or fake the weld, cut or install prompt (ASK F1).
1505	- *Zoom and scale.* The cursor and all world pieces scale on the integer ladder `k` in `[1, k_auto + 2]`; the plate and bar keep HUD pixel size and are re-projected every render frame; a zoom or HUD-scale change mid-channel changes nothing in the simulation (MSA-40, AC-MSA-64).
1506	- *Reduced motion and flashing (HR-8, HR-13).* The bar fill persists, drain and abort snap, the notch hold is kept; the outcome transients may shorten but stay distinguishable by shape (fragments, thinning stream, displaced prop); no element above 3 Hz.
1507	- *Input devices.* The keycap glyph follows Interaction's device latch (classified by event type); both Assembly channels are hold-to-work verbs cancelled by movement or release on every device; a gamepad user holds the same `interact` action (no combo, no radial menu).
1508	- *Accessibility: hold verbs and audio witnesses* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. (1) **Every audio-first witness has a TRUTH visual equivalent.** The weld and cut channels end on sound (the bead settle, the `LOUD` burn-through, the cut's TOOL loop heard through the hull), and the cut-mode witnesses (hiss, creak) are sound-first; each must have a visual equivalent that is also TRUTH and is not a new meter: the LONG bar and work loop already show the actor's own elapsed time, the draught streaks, rim bow and rim frost are visual, the open-valve hiss needs a visual of the same descriptor from Failure & Trail's existing grammar (the lane mist), and the `LOUD` of a cut has a visible equivalent on the crew side of the seam (the spark stream and its stop). Where no visual exists the row is listed as a gap for the accessibility owner, never filled with a number. (2) **The long holds honour a toggle-hold setting.** The 6 s weld, the 4 s cut and the `[VS-B]` veto's hatch hold are hold verbs; with the toggle-hold setting on, one press starts and a second press (or movement) ends the channel, with the same cancel-by-movement rule and the same bar, and nothing about duration, noise or abort changes (ASK AX1). `design/accessibility-requirements.md` does not exist yet; it must be created before the weld story, and these two rules are its first entries (AC-MSA-133, AC-MSA-134). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): X10. The accessibility tier is standard; hold-to-confirm gets a two-tap alternative and an adjustable hold duration. For Assembly the toggle-hold above is the two-tap form of the 6 s weld and 4 s cut; their durations stay sim-fixed (`WELD_CHANNEL_TICKS`, `SECTION_CUT_CHANNEL_TICKS`) and are not made adjustable, because a duration change would change noise per channel; the adjustable hold duration applies to confirm holds such as `CONFIRM_HOLD_S`, which are not Assembly's. `design/accessibility-requirements.md` is to be authored later with `/ux-design accessibility` (noted here, not created by this edit).)*
1509	- *Co-op `[VS-B]`.* Each seat sees its own plate, bar and cursor; a crewmate's channel is visible only as the crewmate's own work loop, sparks and chest beam in the world (the human channel); a MIRROR client plays a cue only per D.17.
1510	- *Engine facts (verified against `docs/engine-reference/godot/`; the reference has no scripting, core, 2D or scene-tree module).* 4.6 dual focus means the plate and bar nodes are non-focusable and mouse-ignoring; 4.7 `CanvasItem` lines carry no feather, so the bar is filled rectangles on the art-px grid (Interaction's ADR candidate); nothing about `Control` theming or world-to-screen projection is asserted here.

In Pre-Production, the specs that must cover it are `design/ux/hud.md` (the three verb plates `verb_weld`, `verb_seam_cut`, `verb_install` and the LONG bar at 9 and 6 ticks per px, via the Interaction UX pass) and the Layout socket-cursor entry in the in-world pattern library (the four-bracket cursor, flat and non-emissive). findings.section: Formulas D.1; MSA-13; Tuning Knobs T17/T18; FB-8; AC-MSA-18
findings.finding: `Q_MIN = max(400, ceil(LEAK_HP/10))` ignores BREACH_HP. BREACH_HP has its own safe range of 1000-6000 (Graph tuning) and LEAK_HP is 2000-6000. With BREACH_HP 6000 and LEAK_HP 4000, a legal q of 400-599 gives hp_seam below BREACH_HP, so a fresh seam can start in BREACH with no tell. That contradicts LSG D.14's own claim ('a fresh seam never starts in LEAK or BREACH'). LSG D.14 already uses the `max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP)` form and registry L5131 records the Graph's pending request. At the defaults (both 4000) the output is identical. Fourth report.
findings.fix: Set Q_MIN = max(400, ceil(max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP) / 10)) in D.1, MSA-13, T17, FB-8 and E-1. Add a boot assertion 10 x Q_MIN >= max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP) and a BREACH_HP row to T18 (1000-6000). Add an AC-MSA-18 fixture: LEAK_HP 4000 with BREACH_HP 6000 and WELD_Q_DEFAULT 500 gives q = 600 and one MSA_Q_CLAMPED. The superset is safe under G4 (identical at defaults).

findings.section: MSA-33; Formulas D.9 note (b) and `ragged_breach_open` row; E-31
findings.finding: The `venting(s)` clause has no ceiling and rests on 'it ends by construction when band_p reaches VACUUM'. That holds only if supply into the keep-side room stays below the outflow at P = 100 dkPa. The outflow at that pressure is k x P, about 4.8 mGU/step at V=20. A live vent, scrubber or O2 tank in a connected life-support loop can hold the room above VACUUM for a long time (the home O2 tank is 3,000,000 mGU). The hull hole has no MVP verb and closing the door does not change `a_hole`, so `venting` stays true. Consequences: the ASSEMBLY_CUT event save stays latched indefinitely, and each interval save defers 7200 ticks and then fires RISKY(ASSEMBLY_BREACH) every interval. E-31 lists only the large-V_total exposure, not the supplied room. The pass-4 note that the supply condition is unstated is still open.
findings.fix: State the condition in D.9 (b) and MSA-33: venting ends only while supply into the room is below k x P_VAC. Then either (a) add a second ceiling for the venting clause (e.g. `VENT_WITHHOLD_MAX_TICKS` >= AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS 7200, with the interval path already capped), or (b) accept the latch and list it in E-31 with the maximum latch duration. Add an AC-MSA-76 fixture with a room that has a live vent and a charged tank, asserting the chosen behaviour.

findings.section: MSA-33; Formulas D.9 (`ragged_breach_open` row and variable `keep_sections`); Dependencies L1; AC-MSA-76/130
findings.finding: `venting(s)` filters `cut_sides` by `keep_sections(s)`, defined as 'Layout `detach_preview`'. `detach_preview` is a pre-cut, ACTIVE-seam prediction (Layout read table; `can_detach` requires ACTIVE), so the term cannot be evaluated once the seam is CUT. That is the only time the predicate matters, including after a restore of a mid-window QUIT or RISKY save. A persisted source exists but is not named: LY-17 gives the leaving component a new body_id from `next_body_id` (INV-7 monotonic), so the keep side is the `cut_sides` entry whose section's `body_of` is the lower body_id (in the MVP, the HOME side). Raised in pass 4 and not fixed.
findings.fix: Define `keep_sections(s)` for a CUT seam from persisted state: sides of `seam_view(s).cut_sides` whose `body_of(section_id)` is the lower body_id of the two bodies produced by the cut (or have the Graph add a `kept` flag). Say explicitly that `detach_preview` is used only at validate time. Add an AC: snapshot mid-vent, restore, and `ragged_breach_open()` and the saved gate inputs recompute to the same value.

findings.section: MSA-33 (worst-case exposure sentence); E-31
findings.finding: The formula is mistyped. `ceil(ln(10) x V_total x 1000 / (2 x 24 x 1000))` has GAS_SCALE in both numerator and denominator, so it evaluates to ceil(5.757) = 6. The stated 5757 steps (34,542 ticks, V_total 120) is the right value from steps = ln(10) / k with k = G_OPEN x A_CUT / (V_total x GAS_SCALE) = 2 x 24 / 120,000. E-31 repeats 34 542.
findings.fix: Rewrite as `ceil( ln(10) x V_total x GAS_SCALE / (G_OPEN x A_CUT x n_holes) )` = ceil(2.302585 x 120 x 1000 / 48) = 5757 steps = 34,542 ticks, and name the symbols.

findings.section: Formulas D.1; MSA-13; Tuning Knobs T17/T18; FB-8; AC-MSA-18
findings.finding: `Q_MIN = max(400, ceil(LEAK_HP/10))` ignores BREACH_HP. BREACH_HP has its own safe range of 1000-6000 (Graph tuning) and LEAK_HP is 2000-6000. With BREACH_HP 6000 and LEAK_HP 4000, a legal q of 400-599 gives hp_seam below BREACH_HP, so a fresh seam can start in BREACH with no tell. That contradicts LSG D.14's own claim ('a fresh seam never starts in LEAK or BREACH'). LSG D.14 already uses the `max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP)` form and registry L5131 records the Graph's pending request. At the defaults (both 4000) the output is identical. Fourth report.
findings.fix: Set Q_MIN = max(400, ceil(max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP) / 10)) in D.1, MSA-13, T17, FB-8 and E-1. Add a boot assertion 10 x Q_MIN >= max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP) and a BREACH_HP row to T18 (1000-6000). findings.section: MSA-33; Formulas D.9 note (b) and `ragged_breach_open` row; E-31
findings.finding: The `venting(s)` clause has no ceiling and rests on 'it ends by construction when band_p reaches VACUUM'. That holds only if supply into the keep-side room stays below the outflow at P = 100 dkPa. The outflow at that pressure is k x P, about 4.8 mGU/step at V=20. A live vent, scrubber or O2 tank in a connected life-support loop can hold the room above VACUUM for a long time (the home O2 tank is 3,000,000 mGU). The hull hole has no MVP verb and closing the door does not change `a_hole`, so `venting` stays true. Consequences: the ASSEMBLY_CUT event save stays latched indefinitely, and each interval save defers 7200 ticks and then fires RISKY(ASSEMBLY_BREACH) every interval. E-31 lists only the large-V_total exposure, not the supplied room. The pass-4 note that the supply condition is unstated is still open.
findings.fix: State the condition in D.9 (b) and MSA-33: venting ends only while supply into the room is below k x P_VAC. Then either (a) add a second ceiling for the venting clause (e.g. `VENT_WITHHOLD_MAX_TICKS` >= AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS 7200, with the interval path already capped), or (b) accept the latch and list it in E-31 with the maximum latch duration. Add an AC-MSA-76 fixture with a room that has a live vent and a charged tank, asserting the chosen behaviour.

A persisted source exists but is not named: LY-17 gives the leaving component a new body_id from `next_body_id` (INV-7 monotonic), so the keep side is the `cut_sides` entry whose section's `body_of` is the lower body_id (in the MVP, the HOME side). findings.section: MSA-33 (worst-case exposure sentence); E-31
findings.finding: The formula is mistyped. `ceil(ln(10) x V_total x 1000 / (2 x 24 x 1000))` has GAS_SCALE in both numerator and denominator, so it evaluates to ceil(5.757) = 6. The stated 5757 steps (34,542 ticks, V_total 120) is the right value from steps = ln(10) / k with k = G_OPEN x A_CUT / (V_total x GAS_SCALE) = 2 x 24 / 120,000. E-31 repeats 34 542.
findings.fix: Rewrite as `ceil( ln(10) x V_total x GAS_SCALE / (G_OPEN x A_CUT x n_holes) )` = ceil(2.302585 x 120 x 1000 / 48) = 5757 steps = 34,542 ticks, and name the symbols.

data.summary: Verdict: APPROVED, no BLOCKING findings. Receipt present, both the GDD and the registry have changed since the last hashes, and all 8 sections are present. Every system in the Dependencies tables has a GDD on disk. The missing prerequisites are the tick-driver ADR and `design/accessibility-requirements.md`, which are tracked as OQ 41 and OQ 34 and are not undesigned systems (R9). The earlier blocking items hold: Option B `pending`, the weep figures, and the D54 predicate are all verified against the Graph, Save/Load and the registry, with the arithmetic recomputed (D.1 table, 382/960-step decompression, 445760 release tick, frame_shift (696, 384), face_octant 5 and 0). The sibling edits from this pass (face_octant, actor_source, BM4 rects, 0/2/4 hook stagger, carry-admitted set, RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK, S3 143 / S4 175) did not break anything; no unconfirmed-decision markers remain. There are 14 RECOMMENDED and 2 NICE items, and the same ones keep coming back. Most important: (1) Assembly's `event_due` settle term conflicts with Save/Load's owner formula (4th report) and the 'Save/Load conforms' claim is false; (2) Q_MIN ignores BREACH_HP (4th report); (3) the `venting` clause has no exit if a vent or tank keeps the room above VACUUM, and `keep_sections` cannot be evaluated after the cut; (4) the exposure formula in MSA-33 is mistyped; (5) stale status rows, line-number citations, 'post_restore clears it', 'five rows', the unowned `cap_duct_junction`, and the one-way IW1 dependency. Findings 1 and 2 should be promoted to BLOCKING if they are not fixed in the next pass. Untestable ACs to rewrite: AC-MSA-130 (ii), AC-MSA-133, AC-MSA-58, AC-MSA-54 and AC-MSA-79. Spike-gated performance criteria and [UNV] coordinates are intentional and were not counted as defects. Nothing found makes implementation wrong or impossible at registry defaults.
